title.zh: 卷六十四 列傳第十四: 高祖二十二子
title.en: Volume 64 Biographies 14: Gaozu's Twenty Two Sons
title.raw: 卷六十四 列傳第十四: 高祖二十二子 Volume 64 Biographies 14: Gaozu's Twenty Two Sons

sentences.zh: 隱太子建成 衛王玄霸 巢王元吉 楚王智雲 荊王元景 漢王元昌 酆王元亨 周王元方 徐王元禮 韓王元嘉 彭王元則 鄭王元懿 霍王元軌 虢王鳳道王元慶 鄧王元裕 舒王元名 魯王靈夔 江王元祥 密王元曉 滕王元嬰

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng; Prince of Wei Xuanba; Prince of Chao Yuanji; Prince of Chu Zhiyun; Prince of Jing Yuanjing; Prince of Han Yuanchang; Prince of Feng Yuanheng; Prince of Zhou Yuanfang; Prince of Xu Yuanli; Prince of Han Yuanjia; Prince of Peng Yuanze; Prince of Zheng Yuanyi; Prince of Huo Yuangui; Prince of Guo Feng; Prince of Dao Yuangqing; Prince of Deng Yuanyu; Prince of Shu Yuanming; Prince of Lu Lingkui; Prince of Jiang Yuanxiang; Prince of Mi Yuanxiao; Prince of Teng Yuanying.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng; the Prince of Wei, Xuanba; the Prince of Chao, Yuanji; the Prince of Chu, Zhiyun; the Prince of Jing, Yuanjing; the Prince of Han, Yuanchang; the Prince of Feng, Yuanheng; the Prince of Zhou, Yuanfang; the Prince of Xu, Yuanli; the Prince of Han, Yuanjia; the Prince of Peng, Yuanze; the Prince of Zheng, Yuanyi; the Prince of Huo, Yuangui; the Prince of Guo, Feng; the Prince of Dao, Yuangqing; the Prince of Deng, Yuanyu; the Prince of Shu, Yuanming; the Prince of Lu, Lingkui; the Prince of Jiang, Yuanxiang; the Prince of Mi, Yuanxiao; and the Prince of Teng, Yuanying.

sentences.zh: 高祖二十二男：太穆皇后生隱太子建成及太宗、衛王玄霸、巢王元吉，萬貴妃生楚王智雲，尹德妃生酆王元亨，莫嬪生荊王元景，孫嬪生漢王元昌，宇文昭儀生韓王元嘉、魯王靈夔，崔嬪生鄧王元裕，楊嬪生江王元祥，小楊嬪生舒王元名，郭婕妤生徐王元禮，劉婕妤生道王元慶，楊美人生虢王鳳，張美人生霍王元軌，張寶林生鄭王元懿，柳寶林生滕王元嬰，王才人生彭王元則，魯才人生密王元曉，張氏生周王元方。

translations.literal: Gaozu had twenty-two sons: Empress Taimu bore the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng, Taizong, Prince of Wei Xuanba, and Prince of Chao Yuanji; Consort Wan Gui bore Prince of Chu Zhiyun; Consort Yin De bore Prince of Feng Yuanheng; Lady Mo bore Prince of Jing Yuanjing; Lady Sun bore Prince of Han Yuanchang; Lady Wen, Zhaoyi, bore Prince of Han Yuanjia and Prince of Lu Lingkui; Lady Cui bore Prince of Deng Yuanyu; Lady Yang bore Prince of Jiang Yuanxiang; Lady Xiao Yang bore Prince of Shu Yuanming; Lady Guo, Jieyu, bore Prince of Xu Yuanli; Lady Liu, Jieyu, bore Prince of Dao Yuangqing; Lady Yang Mei bore Prince of Guo Feng; Lady Zhang Mei bore Prince of Huo Yuangui; Lady Zhang Baolin bore Prince of Zheng Yuanyi; Lady Liu Baolin bore Prince of Teng Yuanying; Lady Wang, Cairen, bore Prince of Peng Yuanze; Lady Lu, Cairen, bore Prince of Mi Yuanxiao; Lady Zhang bore Prince of Zhou Yuanfang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had twenty-two sons. Empress Taimu bore the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng, Taizong, Prince Xuanba of Wei, and Prince Yuanji of Chao. Consort Wan Gui bore Prince Zhiyun of Chu. Consort Yin De bore Prince Yuanheng of Feng. Lady Mo bore Prince Yuanjing of Jing. Lady Sun bore Prince Yuanchang of Han. Lady Wen, a zhaoyi, bore Prince Yuanjia of Han and Prince Lingkui of Lu. Lady Cui bore Prince Yuanyu of Deng. Lady Yang bore Prince Yuanxiang of Jiang. Lady Xiao Yang bore Prince Yuanming of Shu. Lady Guo, a jieyu, bore Prince Yuanli of Xu. Lady Liu, a jieyu, bore Prince Yuangqing of Dao. Lady Yang Mei bore Prince Feng of Guo. Lady Zhang Mei bore Prince Yuangui of Huo. Lady Zhang Baolin bore Prince Yuanyi of Zheng. Lady Liu Baolin bore Prince Yuanying of Teng. Lady Wang, a cairen, bore Prince Yuanze of Peng. Lady Lu, a cairen, bore Prince Yuanxiao of Mi. Lady Zhang bore Prince Yuanfang of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 隱太子建成

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng

sentences.zh: 隱太子建成，高祖長子也。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng was Gaozu's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng was Gaozu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 大業末，高祖捕賊汾、晉，建成攜家屬寄於河東。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, when Gaozu was pursuing bandits in Fen and Jin, Jiancheng took his family and stayed in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye era, while Gaozu was hunting down bandits in Fen and Jin, Jiancheng took his household and lodged them in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 義旗初建，遣使密召之，建成與巢王元吉間行赴太原。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was first raised, he sent envoys to summon Jiancheng in secret; Jiancheng and Prince of Chao Yuanji traveled by hidden routes to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising was first proclaimed, Gaozu sent secret messengers to summon him; Jiancheng and Prince Yuanji of Chao made their way by concealed routes to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 建成至，高祖大喜，拜左領軍大都督，封隴西郡公。

translations.literal: When Jiancheng arrived, Gaozu was greatly pleased and appointed him Grand Commander of the Left Army and enfeoffed him as Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiancheng arrived, Gaozu was overjoyed. He appointed him Grand Commander of the Left Army and enfeoffed him as Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 引兵略西河郡，從平長安。

translations.literal: He led troops to overrun Xihe commandery and followed in the pacification of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops in operations against Xihe commandery and took part in the conquest of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 義寧元年冬，隋恭帝拜唐國世子，開府，置僚屬。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Yining, Emperor Gong of Sui invested him as Heir of the State of Tang, opened a princely establishment, and appointed staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Yining, Emperor Gong of Sui named him heir to the State of Tang, granted him an establishment with full staff, and appointed his officials.

sentences.zh: 二年，授撫軍大將軍、東討元帥，將兵十萬徇洛陽。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Eastern Campaign Commander-in-Chief, leading a hundred thousand troops to advance on Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and commander of the eastern campaign, leading a hundred thousand men against Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及還，恭帝授尚書令。

translations.literal: When he returned, Emperor Gong appointed him Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, Emperor Gong appointed him Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 二年，司竹群盜祝山海有眾一千，自稱護鄉公，詔建成率將軍桑顯和進擊山海，平之。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Sizhu bandit Zhu Shanhai had a following of a thousand men and styled himself Duke Who Protects the District; an edict ordered Jiancheng to lead General Sang Xianhe in an attack on Shanhai, and he was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the Sizhu bandit Zhu Shanhai mustered a thousand followers and proclaimed himself Duke Who Protects the District. An edict ordered Jiancheng to lead General Sang Xianhe against Shanhai, and the rebellion was put down.

sentences.zh: 時涼州人安興貴殺賊帥李軌，以眾來降，令建成往原州應接之。

translations.literal: At that time An Xinggui of Liangzhou killed the rebel leader Li Gui and came to surrender with his forces; Jiancheng was ordered to go to Yuanzhou to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time An Xinggui of Liangzhou killed the rebel leader Li Gui and surrendered with his troops. Jiancheng was sent to Yuanzhou to meet and receive them.

sentences.zh: 時甚暑，而馳獵無度，士卒不堪其勞，逃者過半。

translations.literal: The season was intensely hot, yet he hunted on horseback without limit; the soldiers could not bear the strain, and more than half fled.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was fiercely hot, yet he rode out to hunt without restraint. The troops could not endure the hardship, and more than half deserted.

sentences.zh: 高祖憂其不閒政術，每令習時事，自非軍國大務，悉委決之。

translations.literal: Gaozu worried that he was unskilled in statecraft and had him study current affairs daily; apart from major military and state matters, he entrusted all decisions to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu worried that Jiancheng was unversed in governance and had him study current affairs every day. Aside from major military and state affairs, he entrusted him with full decision-making power.

sentences.zh: 又遣禮部尚書李綱、民部尚書鄭善果俱為宮官，與參謀議。

translations.literal: He also sent Minister of Rites Li Gang and Minister of Revenue Zheng Shanguo as palace officials to deliberate with him.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Minister of Rites Li Gang and Minister of Revenue Zheng Shanguo as palace officials to counsel him in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 四年，稽胡酋帥劉仚成擁部落數萬人為邊害，又詔建成率師討之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Ji Hu chieftain Liu Qian'cheng held several tens of thousands of tribesmen and harried the frontier; again an edict ordered Jiancheng to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Ji Hu chieftain Liu Qian'cheng led tens of thousands of tribesmen in raiding the borderlands. Again an edict ordered Jiancheng to take command against him.

sentences.zh: 軍次鄜州，與仚成軍遇，擊，大破之，斬首數百級，虜獲千餘人。

translations.literal: The army halted at Fuzhou, encountered Qian'cheng's forces, attacked, and routed them utterly, taking several hundred heads and over a thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Fuzhou, met Qian'cheng's forces in battle, and routed them decisively, taking several hundred heads and more than a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 建成設詐放其渠帥數十人，並授官爵，令還本所招慰群胡，仚成與胡中大帥亦請降。

translations.literal: Jiancheng used a ruse to release several dozen of their chieftains, all granting them titles and ranks, and ordered them back to their homes to win over the Hu tribes; Qian'cheng and the great Hu chiefs also asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng devised a stratagem: he released several dozen of their chieftains, invested them with titles and ranks, and sent them back to their people to win over the Hu tribes. Qian'cheng and the senior Hu leaders also petitioned to surrender.

sentences.zh: 建成以胡兵尚眾，恐有變，將盡殺之。

translations.literal: Jiancheng thought the Hu troops were still numerous and feared a revolt; he intended to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng judged that the Hu forces were still too numerous and feared an uprising, so he planned to slaughter them all.

sentences.zh: 乃揚言增置州縣，須有城邑，悉課群胡執板築之具，會築城所，陰勒兵士，皆執之。

translations.literal: He then spread word that new prefectures and counties were to be established and needed walled towns, and levied all the Hu to carry tools for rammed-earth construction; when they gathered at the building site, he secretly ordered the soldiers to seize them all.
translations.idiomatic: He then announced that new prefectures and counties would be established and required walled towns, and levied all the Hu to bring tools for rammed-earth work. When they assembled at the building site, he secretly ordered his soldiers to seize them all.

sentences.zh: 仚成聞有變，奔於梁師都。

translations.literal: Qian'cheng, hearing of the plot, fled to Liang Shidu.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian'cheng learned of the treachery, he fled to Liang Shidu.

sentences.zh: 竟誅降胡六千餘人。

translations.literal: In the end more than six thousand surrendered Hu were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he executed more than six thousand Hu who had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時太宗功業日盛，高祖私許立為太子，建成密知之，乃與齊王元吉潛謀作亂。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong's achievements grew daily, and Gaozu had privately promised to make him crown prince; Jiancheng learned of this in secret and then plotted rebellion with Prince of Qi Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: By then Taizong's achievements were growing daily, and Gaozu had privately promised to make him crown prince. Jiancheng learned of this in secret and conspired with Prince Yuanji of Qi to stage a rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及劉黑闥重反，王珪、魏徵謂建成曰：「殿下但以地居嫡長，爰踐元良，功績既無可稱，仁聲又未遐布。

translations.literal: When Liu Heita rebelled again, Wang Gui and Wei Zheng said to Jiancheng, "Your Highness holds your place only as the legitimate eldest son and has ascended to heir apparent; your achievements are not worth mentioning, and your reputation for benevolence has not spread far.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heita rose in rebellion again, Wang Gui and Wei Zheng said to Jiancheng, "Your Highness holds your position only as the legitimate eldest son who has taken up the role of heir apparent. You have no achievements worth speaking of, and your reputation for benevolence has not spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 而秦王勳業克隆，威震四海，人心所向，殿下何以自安？

translations.literal: Yet the Prince of Qin's merit and enterprise are abundant, his might shakes the four seas, and men's hearts turn to him—how can Your Highness feel secure?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Prince of Qin's achievements are abundant, his prestige shakes the four seas, and the people's hearts turn to him. How can Your Highness feel secure?

sentences.zh: 今黑闥率破亡之餘，眾不盈萬，加以糧運限絕，瘡痍未瘳，若大軍一臨，可不戰而擒也。

translations.literal: Now Heita leads the remnants of the defeated; his forces do not reach ten thousand, grain transport is cut off, and wounds are unhealed—if a great army arrives, he can be taken without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Heita now leads only the shattered remnants of defeat; his forces number fewer than ten thousand, grain supply is cut off, and his wounds are still unhealed. If a great army advances, he can be captured without a battle.

sentences.zh: 願請討之，且以立功，深自封植，因結山東英俊。」

translations.literal: We beg leave to campaign against him, both to win merit and to strengthen your position deeply, and thereby win over the outstanding men of the east."
translations.idiomatic: We urge you to request the campaign against him, both to win merit and to strengthen your own position, and thereby win over the outstanding men of the east."

sentences.zh: 建成從其計，遂請討劉黑闥，擒之而旋。

translations.literal: Jiancheng followed their plan, then requested to campaign against Liu Heita, captured him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng followed their advice, requested the campaign against Liu Heita, captured him, and returned.

sentences.zh: 時高祖晚生諸王，諸母擅寵椒房，親戚並分事宮府，競求恩惠。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu's younger sons by late births had mothers who monopolized favor in the inner quarters; their kin all served the Eastern and Western Palaces in turn and vied for favors.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozu had fathered younger princes late in life, and their mothers monopolized favor in the inner palace. Their relatives all attached themselves to one palace or the other and competed for patronage.

sentences.zh: 太宗每總戎律，惟以撫接才賢為務，至於參請妃媛，素所不行。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizong commanded the armies, he devoted himself solely to winning over men of talent; as for paying court to imperial consorts, he had never done so.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizong held military command, he devoted himself solely to winning over men of talent. As for currying favor with imperial consorts, he had never done so.

sentences.zh: 初平洛陽，高祖遣貴妃等馳往東都選閱宮人及府庫珍物，因私有求索，兼為親族請官。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was first pacified, Gaozu sent consorts and others posthaste to the eastern capital to inspect palace women and treasury treasures; they sought private gain and also requested offices for their kin.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang was first pacified, Gaozu sent consorts and others posthaste to the eastern capital to inspect palace women and treasury treasures. They sought private gain and also requested offices for their relatives.

sentences.zh: 太宗以財簿先已封奏，官爵皆酬有功，並不允許，因此銜恨彌切。

translations.literal: Taizong replied that the account books had already been sealed and submitted, and that offices and ranks were all rewards for merit—he granted none of their requests, and for this their resentment grew keener.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied that the account books had already been sealed and submitted to the throne, and that offices and ranks were rewards for merit alone. He granted none of their requests, and their resentment toward him grew all the sharper.

sentences.zh: 時太宗為陝東道行台，詔於管內得專處分。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong was Director-General of the Shandong Circuit and was issued an edict to exercise sole discretion within his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Taizong served as Director-General of the Shandong Circuit and was authorized by edict to exercise sole discretion within his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通有功，太宗乃給田數十頃。

translations.literal: Prince of Huai'an Shitong had rendered merit, and Taizong granted him several dozen qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shitong of Huai'an had rendered meritorious service, and Taizong granted him several dozen qing of land.

sentences.zh: 後婕妤張氏之父令婕妤私奏以乞其地，高祖手詔賜焉。

translations.literal: Later the father of Jieyu Lady Zhang had her submit a private memorial begging for that land; Gaozu personally issued an edict that it be granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the father of Jieyu Lady Zhang had her submit a private memorial requesting that land. Gaozu personally issued an edict that it be granted to him.

sentences.zh: 神道以教給在前，遂不肯與。

translations.literal: Shitong, on the ground that the grant had been made earlier by edict, refused to yield it.
translations.idiomatic: Shitong, on the ground that the land had already been granted to him by edict, refused to yield it.

sentences.zh: 婕妤矯奏曰：「敕賜妾父地，秦王奪之以與神通。」

translations.literal: The jieyu submitted a false memorial saying, "An edict granted land to my father, but the Prince of Qin seized it and gave it to Shitong."
translations.idiomatic: The jieyu submitted a false memorial, saying, "An edict granted land to my father, but the Prince of Qin seized it and gave it to Shitong."

sentences.zh: 高祖大怒，攘袂責太宗曰：「我詔敕不行，爾之教命，州縣即受。」

translations.literal: Gaozu was furious, rolled up his sleeves, and rebuked Taizong: "My edicts are not obeyed, yet your orders are accepted at once by prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu flew into a rage, rolled up his sleeves, and rebuked Taizong: "My edicts go unheeded, yet your orders are accepted at once by every prefecture and county."

sentences.zh: 他日，高祖呼太宗小名謂裴寂等：「此兒典兵既久，在外專制，為讀書漢所教，非復我昔日子也。」

translations.literal: On another day Gaozu called Taizong by his childhood name and said to Pei Ji and others, "This boy has commanded troops so long that he acts as autocrat abroad; he is taught by bookish men and is no longer the son I once knew."
translations.idiomatic: On another day Gaozu called Taizong by his childhood name and said to Pei Ji and the others, "This boy has held military command so long that he acts as a law unto himself abroad. Bookish men have taught him, and he is no longer the son I once knew."

sentences.zh: 又德妃之父尹阿鼠所為橫恣，秦王府屬杜如晦行經其門，阿鼠家僮數人牽如晦墜馬毆擊之，罵云：「汝是何人，敢經我門而不下馬！」

translations.literal: Moreover, Consort De's father Yin Ashu acted with violent arrogance; Du Ruhui of the Prince of Qin's staff passed his gate, and several of Ashu's household slaves pulled Ruhui from his horse and beat him, cursing, "Who are you to dare pass my gate without dismounting!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Consort De's father Yin Ashu acted with violent arrogance. Du Ruhui, a member of the Prince of Qin's staff, passed his gate, and several of Ashu's household slaves pulled Ruhui from his horse and beat him, crying, "Who are you to dare pass my gate without dismounting!"

sentences.zh: 阿鼠或慮上聞，乃令德妃奏言：「秦王左右凶暴，凌轢妾父。」

translations.literal: Ashu, fearing the emperor might hear of it, had Consort De memorialize: "The Prince of Qin's attendants are brutal and have insulted my father."
translations.idiomatic: Ashu, fearing the emperor might hear of the affair, had Consort De memorialize: "The Prince of Qin's attendants are brutal and have insulted my father."

sentences.zh: 高祖又怒謂太宗曰：「爾之左右，欺我妃嬪之家一至於此，況凡人百姓乎！」

translations.literal: Gaozu again angrily told Taizong, "Your attendants bully the households of my consorts to this degree—what of ordinary people!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu again said angrily to Taizong, "Your attendants bully the households of my consorts to this degree. What must they do to ordinary people!"

sentences.zh: 太宗深自辯明，卒不被納。

translations.literal: Taizong defended himself at length, but in the end his explanations were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong defended himself at length, but in the end his explanations were not accepted.

sentences.zh: 妃嬪等因奏言：「至尊萬歲後，秦王得志，母子定無孑遺。」

translations.literal: The consorts therefore memorialized, "After Your Majesty's ten thousand years, when the Prince of Qin has his way, mother and sons will surely leave no survivor."
translations.idiomatic: The consorts therefore memorialized, "After Your Majesty's ten thousand years, when the Prince of Qin has his way, we and our sons will surely leave no survivor."

sentences.zh: 因悲泣哽咽。

translations.literal: They wept in grief, choked with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: They wept in grief, choked with sobs.

sentences.zh: 又云：「東宮慈厚，必能養育妾母子。」

translations.literal: They also said, "The Eastern Palace is kind and generous and will surely nurture us, mother and sons."
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "The Eastern Palace is kind and generous and will surely nurture us, mother and sons."

sentences.zh: 高祖惻愴久之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was moved to compassion for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was moved to compassion for a long while.

sentences.zh: 自是於太宗恩禮漸薄，廢立之心亦以此定，建成、元吉轉蒙恩寵。

translations.literal: From then on his favor and courtesy toward Taizong grew thin, and his mind to depose and establish was thereby settled; Jiancheng and Yuanji in turn received his grace and favor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his favor toward Taizong grew thin, and his mind to depose and establish an heir was thereby settled. Jiancheng and Yuanji in turn received his grace and favor.

sentences.zh: 自武德初，高祖令太宗居西宮之承乾殿，元吉居武德殿後院，與上台、東宮晝夜並通，更無限隔。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Wude, Gaozu had Taizong reside in Chengqian Hall of the Western Palace and Yuanji in the rear court of Wude Hall; they communicated day and night with the Supreme Palace and Eastern Palace without any barrier.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning of Wude, Gaozu had Taizong reside in Chengqian Hall of the Western Palace and Yuanji in the rear court of Wude Hall. Day and night they passed freely to the Supreme Palace and the Eastern Palace without any barrier between them.

sentences.zh: 皇太子及二王出入上台，皆乘馬攜弓刀雜用之物，相遇則如家人之禮。

translations.literal: The crown prince and the two princes, entering and leaving the Supreme Palace, all rode horses and carried bows, blades, and miscellaneous gear; when they met, they observed the etiquette of family members.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the two princes, entering and leaving the Supreme Palace, all rode horses and carried bows, blades, and assorted gear. When they met, they observed the informal etiquette of family members.

sentences.zh: 由是皇太子令及秦、齊二王教與詔敕並行，百姓惶惑，莫知准的。

translations.literal: Hence the crown prince's orders and the instructions and edicts of the Princes of Qin and Qi circulated together; the people were alarmed and did not know which standard to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the crown prince's orders and the instructions and edicts of the Princes of Qin and Qi circulated side by side. The people were alarmed and did not know which authority to obey.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉又外結小人，內連嬖倖，高祖所寵張婕妤、尹德妃皆與之淫亂。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji also allied outwardly with petty men and inwardly with favorites; Jieyu Lady Zhang and Consort Yin De, whom Gaozu favored, both had illicit relations with them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji also allied outwardly with petty men and inwardly with palace favorites. Jieyu Lady Zhang and Consort Yin De, whom Gaozu favored, both had illicit relations with them.

sentences.zh: 復與諸公主及六宮親戚驕恣縱橫，並兼田宅，侵奪犬馬。

translations.literal: They also joined with the princesses and the kin of the six palaces in arrogant license, seizing fields and houses together and plundering dogs and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They also joined with the princesses and the kin of the six palaces in arrogant license, seizing fields and houses together and plundering livestock.

sentences.zh: 同惡相濟，掩蔽聰明，苟行己志，惟以甘言諛辭承候顏色。

translations.literal: Evil men aided one another, obscured Gaozu's clear judgment, indulged their own wills, and offered only sweet words and flattery to attend his mood.
translations.idiomatic: Evil men aided one another, obscured Gaozu's clear judgment, indulged their own wills, and offered only sweet words and flattery to attend his mood.

sentences.zh: 建成乃私召四方驍勇，並募長安惡少年二千餘人，畜為宮甲，分屯左、右長林門，號為長林兵。

translations.literal: Jiancheng then secretly summoned fierce warriors from the four quarters and also recruited more than two thousand vicious youths of Chang'an, kept them as palace guards, stationed them at the left and right Changlin Gates, and called them the Changlin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng then secretly summoned fierce warriors from the four quarters and recruited more than two thousand vicious youths of Chang'an. He kept them as palace guards, stationed them at the left and right Changlin Gates, and called them the Changlin Army.

sentences.zh: 及高祖幸仁智宮，留建成居守，建成先令慶州總管楊文干募健兒送京師，欲以為變。

translations.literal: When Gaozu visited Renzhi Palace, he left Jiancheng to hold the capital; Jiancheng first ordered Qingzhou Inspector-General Yang Wengan to recruit stalwart men and send them to the capital, intending to use them for a coup.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu visited Renzhi Palace, he left Jiancheng to hold the capital. Jiancheng first ordered Qingzhou Inspector-General Yang Wengan to recruit stalwart men and send them to the capital, intending to use them for a coup.

sentences.zh: 又遣郎將爾硃煥、校尉橋公山齎甲以賜文干，令起兵共相應接。

translations.literal: He also sent Commandant Erzhu Huan and Captain Qiao Gongshan bearing armor as gifts to Wengan, ordering him to raise troops in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Commandant Erzhu Huan and Captain Qiao Gongshan bearing armor as gifts to Wengan, ordering him to raise troops in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 公山、煥等行至豳鄉，懼罪馳告其事。

translations.literal: Gongshan, Huan, and the others reached Bin township, feared punishment, and galloped to report the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshan, Huan, and the others reached Bin township, feared punishment, and galloped to report the affair.

sentences.zh: 高祖托以他事，手詔追建成詣行在所。

translations.literal: Gaozu used another matter as pretext and personally issued an edict Jiancheng to come to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu used another matter as pretext and personally issued an edict Jiancheng to come to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 既至，高祖大怒，建成叩頭謝罪，奮身自投於地，幾至於絕。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Gaozu was furious; Jiancheng kowtowed in confession, threw himself to the ground with abandon, and nearly lost consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Gaozu was furious. Jiancheng kowtowed in confession, threw himself to the ground, and nearly lost consciousness.

sentences.zh: 其夜，置之幕中，令殿中監陳萬福防禦，而文干遂舉兵反。

translations.literal: That night he was placed in a tent and Palace Supervisor Chen Wanfu was ordered to guard him; meanwhile Wengan raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was placed in a tent and Palace Supervisor Chen Wanfu was ordered to guard him. Meanwhile Wengan raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 高祖馳使召太宗以謀之，太宗曰：「文干小豎狂悖，起兵州府，官司已應擒剿。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent swift messengers to summon Taizong to consult him; Taizong said, "Wengan is a petty fellow, mad and rebellious; he has raised troops in the prefectures, and the officials should already be capturing and suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent swift messengers to summon Taizong to consult him. Taizong said, "Wengan is a petty fellow, mad and rebellious. He has raised troops in the prefectures, and the officials should already be capturing and suppressing him.

sentences.zh: 縱其假息時刻，但須遣一將耳。」

translations.literal: Even if he gains a moment's respite, one need only send a single general."
translations.idiomatic: Even if he gains a moment's respite, one need only send a single general."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「文幹事連建成，恐應之者眾，汝宜自行，還，立汝為太子。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Wengan's affair is linked to Jiancheng; I fear many will respond. You should go yourself; when you return, I will establish you as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Wengan's affair is linked to Jiancheng, and I fear many will rally to him. You should go yourself. When you return, I will establish you as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 吾不能效隋文帝誅殺骨肉，廢建成封作蜀王，地既僻小易制。

translations.literal: I cannot imitate Emperor Wen of Sui in executing my own flesh and blood; I will depose Jiancheng and enfeoff him as Prince of Shu—the territory is remote and small and easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot imitate Emperor Wen of Sui in executing my own flesh and blood. I will depose Jiancheng and enfeoff him as Prince of Shu—the territory is remote and small and easy to control.

sentences.zh: 若不能事汝，亦易取耳。」

translations.literal: If he cannot serve you, he will be easy to remove as well."
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot serve you, he will be easy to remove as well."

sentences.zh: 太宗既行，元吉及四妃更為建成內請，封倫又外為遊說，高祖意便頓改，遂寢不行，復令建成還京居守。

translations.literal: After Taizong had set out, Yuanji and the four consorts again pleaded inwardly for Jiancheng, and Feng Lun lobbied outwardly; Gaozu's mind abruptly changed, the plan was shelved, and Jiancheng was again ordered back to the capital to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong had set out, Yuanji and the four consorts again pleaded inwardly for Jiancheng, and Feng Lun lobbied outwardly. Gaozu's mind abruptly changed, the plan was shelved, and Jiancheng was again ordered back to the capital to hold it.

sentences.zh: 惟責以兄弟不能相容，歸罪於中允王珪、左衛率韋挺及天策兵曹杜淹等，並流之巂州。

translations.literal: He only blamed them for brothers' inability to tolerate one another, laid the fault on Palace Companion Wang Gui, Left Guard Commander Wei Ting, and Heavenly Stratagem Army Clerk Du Yan, and exiled them all to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He only blamed them for the brothers' inability to tolerate one another, laid the fault on Palace Companion Wang Gui, Left Guard Commander Wei Ting, and Heavenly Stratagem Army Clerk Du Yan, and exiled them all to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 後又與元吉謀行鴆毒，引太宗入宮夜宴，既而太宗心中暴痛，吐血數升，淮安王神通狼狽扶還西宮。

translations.literal: Later they again plotted with Yuanji to use poisoned wine, drew Taizong into the palace for a night banquet, and then Taizong suffered sudden violent pain in the chest and vomited several sheng of blood; Prince of Huai'an Shitong helped him back to the Western Palace in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Later they again plotted with Yuanji to use poisoned wine and drew Taizong into the palace for a night banquet. Taizong then suffered sudden violent pain in the chest and vomited several sheng of blood. Prince Shitong of Huai'an helped him back to the Western Palace in disarray.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸第問疾，因敕建成：「秦王素不能飲，更勿夜聚。」

translations.literal: Gaozu visited his residence to inquire after his illness and thereupon charged Jiancheng, "The Prince of Qin has never been able to hold his wine—do not gather at night again."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu visited his residence to inquire after his illness and thereupon charged Jiancheng, "The Prince of Qin has never been able to hold his wine. Do not gather at night again."

sentences.zh: 乃謂太宗曰：「發跡晉陽，本是汝計；

translations.literal: He then said to Taizong, "Our rise from Jinyang was originally your plan;
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Taizong, "Our rise from Jinyang was originally your plan;

sentences.zh: 克平宇內，是汝大功。

translations.literal: the conquest and pacification of the realm are your great merit.
translations.idiomatic: the conquest and pacification of the realm are your great merit.

sentences.zh: 欲升儲位，汝固讓不受，以成汝美志。

translations.literal: I wished to raise you to the heirship, but you firmly declined and would not accept, thereby fulfilling your noble wish.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to raise you to the heirship, but you firmly declined, thereby fulfilling your noble wish.

sentences.zh: 建成自居東宮，多歷年所，今復不忍奪之。

translations.literal: Jiancheng has dwelt in the Eastern Palace for many years; now I again cannot bear to take it from him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng has dwelt in the Eastern Palace for many years. Now I again cannot bear to take it from him.

sentences.zh: 觀汝兄弟是不和，同在京邑，必有忿競。

translations.literal: Seeing that you brothers are not in harmony, if you remain together in the capital there will surely be angry rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that you brothers are not in harmony, if you remain together in the capital there will surely be angry rivalry.

sentences.zh: 汝還行台，居於洛陽，自陝已東，悉宜主之。

translations.literal: Return to your directorate and reside in Luoyang; from Shan eastward, you should hold sway over all.
translations.idiomatic: Return to your directorate and reside in Luoyang. From Shan eastward, you should hold sway over all.

sentences.zh: 仍令汝建天子旌旗，如梁孝王故事。」

translations.literal: I will further let you raise the Son of Heaven's banners, following the precedent of Prince Xiao of Liang."
translations.idiomatic: I will further let you raise the Son of Heaven's banners, following the precedent of Prince Xiao of Liang."

sentences.zh: 太宗泣而奏曰：「今日之授，實非所願，不能遠離膝下。」

translations.literal: Taizong wept as he replied, "This grant today is truly not what I wish; I cannot bear to be far from Your Majesty's knee."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wept as he replied, "This grant today is truly not what I wish. I cannot bear to be far from Your Majesty's knee."

sentences.zh: 言訖嗚咽，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: When he had spoken he sobbed, overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he had spoken he sobbed, overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「昔陸賈漢臣，尚有遞過之事，況吾四方之主，天下為家。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "In former times the Han minister Lu Jia still had occasions of passing back and forth—how much more so for me, lord of the four quarters, with all under Heaven as my household.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "In former times the Han minister Lu Jia still had occasions of passing back and forth. How much more so for me, lord of the four quarters, with all under Heaven as my household.

sentences.zh: 東西兩宮，途路咫尺，憶汝即往，無勞悲也。」

translations.literal: The Eastern and Western Palaces are but a foot's journey apart; when I think of you I can go at once—do not grieve needlessly."
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern and Western Palaces are but a foot's journey apart. When I think of you I can go at once—do not grieve needlessly."

sentences.zh: 及將行，建成、元吉相與謀曰：「秦王今往洛陽，既得土地甲兵，必為後患。

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, Jiancheng and Yuanji plotted together, saying, "If the Prince of Qin now goes to Luoyang and gains land and armor and troops, he will surely become a future threat.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to depart, Jiancheng and Yuanji plotted together, saying, "If the Prince of Qin now goes to Luoyang and gains land, armor, and troops, he will surely become a future threat.

sentences.zh: 留在京師，制之一匹夫耳。」

translations.literal: Keep him in the capital, and he is controlled as a mere commoner."
translations.idiomatic: Keep him in the capital, and he is controlled as a mere commoner."

sentences.zh: 密令數人上封事曰：「秦王左右多是東人，聞往洛陽，非常欣躍，觀其情狀，自今一去，不作來意。」

translations.literal: They secretly ordered several men to submit sealed memorials saying, "Most of the Prince of Qin's attendants are men of the east; hearing that he is going to Luoyang, they are extraordinarily joyful. Judging from their manner, once he leaves he will not intend to return."
translations.idiomatic: They secretly ordered several men to submit sealed memorials saying, "Most of the Prince of Qin's attendants are men of the east. Hearing that he is going to Luoyang, they are extraordinarily joyful. Judging from their manner, once he leaves he will not intend to return."

sentences.zh: 高祖於是遂停。

translations.literal: Gaozu thereupon halted the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thereupon halted the plan.

sentences.zh: 是後，日夜陰與元吉連結後宮，譖訴愈切，高祖惑之。

translations.literal: After this they joined with Yuanji day and night in secret with the inner palace; their slanders grew ever sharper, and Gaozu was misled.
translations.idiomatic: After this they joined with Yuanji day and night in secret with the inner palace. Their slanders grew ever sharper, and Gaozu was misled.

sentences.zh: 太宗懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: Taizong was afraid and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was afraid and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 李靖、李勣等數言：「大王以功高被疑，靖等請申犬馬之力。」

translations.literal: Li Jing, Li Ji, and others repeatedly said, "Great Prince, because your merit is high you are suspected; we beg to exert the strength of dogs and horses."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, Li Ji, and others repeatedly said, "Great Prince, because your merit is high you are suspected. We beg to exert the strength of dogs and horses on your behalf."

sentences.zh: 封倫亦潛勸太宗圖之，並不許。

translations.literal: Feng Lun also secretly urged Taizong to plot against them, but he would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun also secretly urged Taizong to plot against them, but he would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 倫反言於高祖曰：「秦王恃有大勳，不服居太子之下。

translations.literal: Lun then spoke to Gaozu in turn, saying, "The Prince of Qin relies on his great merit and will not submit to serving below the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Lun then spoke to Gaozu in turn, saying, "The Prince of Qin relies on his great merit and will not submit to serving below the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 若不立之，願早為之所。」

translations.literal: If you do not establish him, I beg you to deal with the matter early."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not establish him, I beg you to deal with the matter early."

sentences.zh: 又說建成作亂，曰：「夫為四海者，不顧其親。

translations.literal: He also urged Jiancheng to rebel, saying, "One who holds the four seas does not heed his kin.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Jiancheng to rebel, saying, "One who holds the four seas does not heed his kin.

sentences.zh: 漢高乞羹，此之謂矣。」

translations.literal: When the Founder of Han begged for broth—that is what is meant."
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder of Han begged for broth—that is what is meant."

sentences.zh: 九年，突厥犯邊，詔元吉率師拒之，元吉因兵集，將與建成剋期舉事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Turks invaded the frontier; an edict ordered Yuanji to lead troops against them. Yuanji, because troops were assembling, planned with Jiancheng to rise on a set date.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Turks invaded the frontier, and an edict ordered Yuanji to lead troops against them. With troops assembling, Yuanji planned with Jiancheng to rise on a set date.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、房玄齡、杜如晦、尉遲敬德、侯君集等日夜固爭曰：「事急矣！

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yuchi Jingde, Hou Junji, and others argued day and night, saying, "The matter is urgent!
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yuchi Jingde, Hou Junji, and others argued day and night, saying, "The matter is urgent!

sentences.zh: 若不行權道，社稷必危。

translations.literal: If you do not take the expedient course, the altars of state will surely be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not take the expedient course, the altars of state will surely be in peril.

sentences.zh: 周公聖人，豈無情於骨肉？

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou was a sage—did he lack feeling for his kin?
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou was a sage—did he lack feeling for his kin?

sentences.zh: 為存社稷，大義滅親。

translations.literal: To preserve the altars of state, he extinguished kin for the greater righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: To preserve the altars of state, he extinguished kin for the greater righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今大王臨機不斷，坐受屠戮，於義何成？

translations.literal: Now, Great Prince, you hesitate at the critical moment and sit waiting to be slaughtered—how can righteousness be fulfilled?
translations.idiomatic: Great Prince, you hesitate at the critical moment and sit waiting to be slaughtered. How can righteousness be fulfilled?

sentences.zh: 若不見聽，無忌等將竄身草澤，不得居王左右。」

translations.literal: If you will not heed us, Wuji and the others will flee into the marshes and cannot remain at your side."
translations.idiomatic: If you will not heed us, Wuji and the others will flee into the marshes and cannot remain at your side."

sentences.zh: 太宗然其計。

translations.literal: Taizong approved their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved their plan.

sentences.zh: 六月三日，密奏建成、元吉淫亂後宮，因自陳曰：「臣於兄弟無絲毫所負，今欲殺臣，似為世充、建德報仇。

translations.literal: On the third day of the sixth month he secretly memorialized that Jiancheng and Yuanji had debauched the inner palace, and stated himself: "I have not failed my brothers in the slightest; now they wish to kill me, as if to avenge Shimin and Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the sixth month he secretly memorialized that Jiancheng and Yuanji had debauched the inner palace, and stated himself, "I have not failed my brothers in the slightest. Now they wish to kill me, as if to avenge Shimin and Jiande.

sentences.zh: 臣今枉死，永違君親，魂歸地下，實亦恥見諸賊。」

translations.literal: If I must die unjustly now, I shall forever be parted from my sovereign and kin; returning in spirit to the underworld, I would indeed be ashamed to face those villains."
translations.idiomatic: If I must die unjustly now, I shall forever be parted from my sovereign and kin. Returning in spirit to the underworld, I would indeed be ashamed to face those villains."

sentences.zh: 高祖省之愕然，報曰：「明日當勘問，汝宜早參。」

translations.literal: Gaozu read it and was startled; he replied, "Tomorrow I shall investigate; you should attend early."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read it and was startled. He replied, "Tomorrow I shall investigate. You should attend early."

sentences.zh: 四日，太宗將左右九人至玄武門自衛。

translations.literal: On the fourth day Taizong brought nine attendants to Xuanwu Gate to guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day Taizong brought nine attendants to Xuanwu Gate to guard himself.

sentences.zh: 高祖已召裴寂、蕭瑀、陳叔達、封倫、宇文士及、竇誕、顏師古等，欲令窮覆其事。

translations.literal: Gaozu had already summoned Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, Feng Lun, Yuwen Shiji, Dou Yan, Yan Shigu, and others, intending to have them thoroughly investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had already summoned Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, Feng Lun, Yuwen Shiji, Dou Yan, Yan Shigu, and others, intending to have them thoroughly investigate the matter.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉行至臨湖殿，覺變，即回馬，將東歸宮府。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji reached Linhu Hall, sensed that something was amiss, turned their horses at once, and were about to return east to their palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji reached Linhu Hall, sensed that something was amiss, turned their horses at once, and were about to return east to their palaces.

sentences.zh: 太宗隨而呼之，元吉馬上張弓，再三不彀。

translations.literal: Taizong followed and called to them; Yuanji drew his bow on horseback but could not fully draw it after several tries.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong followed and called to them. Yuanji drew his bow on horseback but could not fully draw it after several tries.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃射之，建成應弦而斃，元吉中流矢而走，尉遲敬德殺之。

translations.literal: Taizong then shot at them; Jiancheng fell dead at the twang of the bowstring, Yuanji was struck by a flying arrow and fled, and Yuchi Jingde killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then shot at them. Jiancheng fell dead at the twang of the bowstring. Yuanji was struck by a flying arrow and fled, and Yuchi Jingde killed him.

sentences.zh: 俄而東宮及齊府精兵二千人結陣馳攻玄武門，守門兵仗拒之，不得入，良久接戰，流矢及於內殿。

translations.literal: Soon two thousand elite troops of the Eastern Palace and Qi establishment formed ranks and galloped to attack Xuanwu Gate; the gate guards with weapons repelled them and they could not enter. After a long while fighting continued, and stray arrows reached the inner halls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon two thousand elite troops of the Eastern Palace and Qi establishment formed ranks and galloped to attack Xuanwu Gate. The gate guards with weapons repelled them and they could not enter. After a long while fighting continued, and stray arrows reached the inner halls.

sentences.zh: 太宗左右數百騎來赴難，建成等兵遂敗散。

translations.literal: Several hundred horsemen of Taizong's attendants came to the rescue, and Jiancheng's troops were defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred horsemen of Taizong's attendants came to the rescue, and Jiancheng's troops were defeated and scattered.

sentences.zh: 高祖大驚，謂裴寂等曰：「今日之事如何？」

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly alarmed and said to Pei Ji and the others, "What is to be done about today's affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was greatly alarmed and said to Pei Ji and the others, "What is to be done about today's affair?"

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀、陳叔達進曰：「臣聞內外無限，父子不親，當斷不斷，反受其亂。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu and Chen Shuda advanced and said, "We have heard that when inner and outer have no bounds and father and son are not close, one who should cut off but does not will suffer disorder in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu and Chen Shuda advanced and said, "We have heard that when inner and outer have no bounds and father and son are not close, one who should cut off but does not will suffer disorder in turn.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉，義旗草創之際，並不預謀；

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji, at the time the righteous banner was first raised, took no part in the planning;
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji, at the time the righteous banner was first raised, took no part in the planning.

sentences.zh: 建立已來，又無功德，常自懷憂，相濟為惡，釁起蕭牆，遂有今日之事。

translations.literal: since the establishment they have had no merit, constantly harbored anxiety, aided one another in evil, and raised trouble within the palace walls—hence today's affair.
translations.idiomatic: Since the establishment they have had no merit, constantly harbored anxiety, aided one another in evil, and raised trouble within the palace walls—hence today's affair.

sentences.zh: 秦王功蓋天下，率土歸心，若處以元良，委之國務，陛下如釋重負，蒼生自然乂安。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin's merit covers all under Heaven; the realm turns to him in heart. If he is placed as heir apparent and entrusted with state affairs, Your Majesty will be as one who has laid down a heavy burden, and the people will naturally be at peace."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin's merit covers all under Heaven; the realm turns to him in heart. If he is placed as heir apparent and entrusted with state affairs, Your Majesty will be as one who has laid down a heavy burden, and the people will naturally be at peace."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「善！

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Good!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Good!

sentences.zh: 此亦吾之夙志也。」

translations.literal: This too has long been my own wish."
translations.idiomatic: This too has long been my own wish."

sentences.zh: 乃命召太宗而撫之曰：「近日已來，幾有投杼之惑。」

translations.literal: He then ordered Taizong summoned and comforted him, saying, "In recent days I have nearly had the confusion of casting aside the pestle."
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Taizong summoned and comforted him, saying, "In recent days I have nearly had the confusion of casting aside the pestle."

sentences.zh: 太宗哀號久之。

translations.literal: Taizong wailed for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wailed for a long while.

sentences.zh: 建成死時年三十八。

translations.literal: Jiancheng was thirty-eight years old at his death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng was thirty-eight years old at his death.

sentences.zh: 長子太原王承宗早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son, Prince of Taiyuan Chengzong, died early.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Prince Chengzong of Taiyuan, died early.

sentences.zh: 次子安陸王承道、河東王承德、武安王承訓、汝南王承明、鉅鹿王承義並坐誅。

translations.literal: His second sons Prince of Anlu Chengdong, Prince of Hedong Chengde, Prince of Wu'an Cheng Xun, Prince of Runan Chengming, and Prince of Julu Chengyi were all executed on account of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: His second sons Prince Chengdong of Anlu, Prince Chengde of Hedong, Prince Cheng Xun of Wu'an, Prince Chengming of Runan, and Prince Chengyi of Julu were all executed on account of the affair.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，追封建成為息王，謚曰隱，以禮改葬。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Jiancheng as Prince of Xi and gave him the posthumous title Hidden, reinterring him with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Jiancheng as Prince of Xi and gave him the posthumous title Hidden, reinterring him with full rites.

sentences.zh: 葬日，太宗於宜秋門哭之甚哀，仍以皇子趙王福為建成嗣。

translations.literal: On the day of the burial Taizong wept bitterly at Yichiu Gate and made Prince Zhao Fu his heir in Jiancheng's line.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the burial Taizong wept bitterly at Yichiu Gate and made Prince Zhao Fu his heir in Jiancheng's line.

sentences.zh: 十六年五月，又追贈皇太子，謚仍依舊。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year he again posthumously invested him as crown prince; the posthumous title remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year he again posthumously invested him as crown prince; the posthumous title remained as before.

sentences.zh: 衛王玄霸

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Xuanba.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuanba of Wei

sentences.zh: 巢王元吉

translations.literal: Prince of Chao Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanji of Chao

sentences.zh: 巢王元吉，高祖第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Chao Yuanji was Gaozu's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanji of Chao was Gaozu's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 義師起，授太原郡守，封姑臧郡公。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, he was appointed Administrator of Taiyuan commandery and enfeoffed as Duke of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, he was appointed Administrator of Taiyuan commandery and enfeoffed as Duke of Guzang.

sentences.zh: 尋進封齊國公，授十五郡諸軍事、鎮北大將軍，留鎮太原，許以便宜行事。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Duke of Qi, given command over military affairs in fifteen commanderies as Grand General Who Pacifies the North, left to hold Taiyuan, and permitted to act at his own discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to Duke of Qi, given command over military affairs in fifteen commanderies as Grand General Who Pacifies the North, left to hold Taiyuan, and permitted to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，進爵為王，授并州總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was advanced to prince and appointed Inspector-General of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he was advanced to prince and appointed Inspector-General of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，劉武周南侵汾、晉，詔遣右衛將軍宇文歆助元吉守并州。

translations.literal: In the second year Liu Wuzhou invaded south into Fen and Jin; an edict ordered Right Guard General Yuwen Xin to assist Yuanji in holding Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Liu Wuzhou invaded south into Fen and Jin. An edict ordered Right Guard General Yuwen Xin to assist Yuanji in holding Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元吉性好畋獵，載網罟三十餘兩，嘗言「我寧三日不食，不能一日不獵」，又縱其左右攘奪百姓。

translations.literal: Yuanji was fond of hunting; he carried more than thirty sets of nets and snares, and once said, "I would rather go three days without food than one day without hunting." He also let his attendants plunder the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was fond of hunting. He carried more than thirty sets of nets and snares and once said, "I would rather go three days without food than one day without hunting." He also let his attendants plunder the common people.

sentences.zh: 歆頻諫不納，乃上表曰：「王在州之日，多出微行，常共竇誕遊獵，蹂踐谷稼，放縱親暱，公行攘奪，境內六畜，因之殆盡。

translations.literal: Xin repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded; he then submitted a memorial saying, "While the prince was in the prefecture he often went out incognito, constantly hunting with Dou Yan, trampling the grain in the fields, indulging his intimates, openly seizing goods, until the livestock within the borders were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Xin repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded. He then submitted a memorial saying, "While the prince was in the prefecture he often went out incognito, constantly hunting with Dou Yan, trampling the grain in the fields, indulging his intimates, and openly seizing goods until the livestock within the borders were nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 當衢而射，觀人避箭以為笑樂。

translations.literal: He would shoot in the middle of the road and laugh to see people dodge his arrows.
translations.idiomatic: He would shoot in the middle of the road and laugh to see people dodge his arrows.

sentences.zh: 分遣左右，戲為攻戰，至相擊刺毀傷至死。

translations.literal: He sent his attendants to play at battle, until they stabbed and wounded one another to death.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his attendants to play at battle until they stabbed and wounded one another to death.

sentences.zh: 夜開府門，宣淫他室。

translations.literal: At night he opened the princely gates and debauched other men's wives.
translations.idiomatic: At night he opened the princely gates and debauched other men's wives.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨毒，各懷憤嘆。

translations.literal: The people hated him and each harbored bitter sighs.
translations.idiomatic: The people hated him and each harbored bitter sighs.

sentences.zh: 以此守城，安能自保！」

translations.literal: With such a man defending the city, how can he protect himself!"
translations.idiomatic: With such a man defending the city, how can he protect himself!"

sentences.zh: 元吉竟坐免。

translations.literal: Yuanji was dismissed from office on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was dismissed from office on this account.

sentences.zh: 又諷父老詣闕請之，尋令復職。

translations.literal: He also prompted the elders to go to the palace gate to request his restoration, and before long he was ordered back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He also prompted the elders to go to the palace gate to request his restoration, and before long he was ordered back to his post.

sentences.zh: 時劉武週率五千騎至黃蛇嶺，元吉遣車騎將軍張達以步卒百人先嘗之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Wuzhou led five thousand horsemen to Huangshe Ridge; Yuanji sent Cavalry General Zhang Da with a hundred foot soldiers to test them first.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Wuzhou led five thousand horsemen to Huangshe Ridge. Yuanji sent Cavalry General Zhang Da with a hundred foot soldiers to test them first.

sentences.zh: 達以步卒少，固請不行。

translations.literal: Da said the foot soldiers were too few and firmly refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Da said the foot soldiers were too few and firmly refused to go.

sentences.zh: 元吉強遣之，至則盡沒於賊。

translations.literal: Yuanji forced him to go; when he arrived he was entirely destroyed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji forced him to go. When he arrived he was entirely destroyed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 達憤怒，因引武周攻陷榆次，進逼并州。

translations.literal: Da, in anger, then led Wuzhou to take Yuci and advance against Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Da, in anger, then led Wuzhou to take Yuci and advance against Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元吉大懼，紿其司馬劉德威曰：「卿以老弱守城，吾以強兵出戰。」

translations.literal: Yuanji was greatly afraid and deceived his Chief Administrator Liu Dewei, saying, "You hold the city with the old and weak; I will go out to battle with strong troops."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was greatly afraid and deceived his Chief Administrator Liu Dewei, saying, "You hold the city with the old and weak. I will go out to battle with strong troops.

sentences.zh: 因夜出兵，攜其妻妾棄軍奔還京師，并州遂陷。

translations.literal: He then led troops out by night, took his wives and concubines, abandoned the army, and fled back to the capital; Bingzhou was lost.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops out by night, took his wives and concubines, abandoned the army, and fled back to the capital. Bingzhou was lost.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒甚，謂禮部尚書李綱曰：「元吉幼小，未習時事，故遣竇誕、宇文歆輔之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was furious and said to Minister of Rites Li Gang, "Yuanji is young and has not learned current affairs, so I sent Dou Yan and Yuwen Xin to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was furious and said to Minister of Rites Li Gang, "Yuanji is young and has not learned current affairs, so I sent Dou Yan and Yuwen Xin to assist him.

sentences.zh: 強兵數萬，食支十年，起義興運之基，一朝而棄。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of strong troops, provisions for ten years—the foundation of our righteous rising—were abandoned in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of strong troops and provisions for ten years—the foundation of our righteous rising—were abandoned in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 宇文歆首畫此計，我當斬之。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Xin first devised this plan; I ought to execute him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin first devised this plan. I ought to execute him."

sentences.zh: 綱曰：「賴歆令陛下不失愛子，臣以為有功。」

translations.literal: Gang said, "Thanks to Xin, Your Majesty did not lose a beloved son; I consider that a merit."
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "Thanks to Xin, Your Majesty did not lose a beloved son. I consider that a merit."

sentences.zh: 高祖問其故，綱封曰：「罪由竇誕不能規諷，致令軍人怨憤。

translations.literal: Gaozu asked the reason; Gang sealed his lips and said, "The fault lies with Dou Yan's failure to admonish and correct, which caused the soldiers' resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked the reason. Gang sealed his lips and said, "The fault lies with Dou Yan's failure to admonish and correct, which caused the soldiers' resentment.

sentences.zh: 又齊王年少，肆行驕逸，放縱左右，侵漁百姓。

translations.literal: Moreover the Prince of Qi is young and acts with arrogant license, indulging his attendants and encroaching on the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Prince of Qi is young and acts with arrogant license, indulging his attendants and encroaching on the common people.

sentences.zh: 誕曾無諫止，乃隨順掩藏，以成其釁，此誕之罪。

translations.literal: Yan never once remonstrated but followed along and concealed the facts, thereby completing the disaster—this is Yan's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yan never once remonstrated but followed along and concealed the facts, thereby completing the disaster—this is Yan's fault.

sentences.zh: 宇文歆論情則疏，向彼又淺，王之過失，悉以聞奏。

translations.literal: Yuwen Xin, judged by affection, was distant, and toward the prince he was shallow; yet he reported all the prince's faults to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin, judged by affection, was distant, and toward the prince he was shallow. Yet he reported all the prince's faults to the throne.

sentences.zh: 且父子之際，人所難言，而歆言之，豈非忠懇？

translations.literal: Between father and son, what is hard for anyone to speak—yet Xin spoke of it. Was that not loyal earnestness?
translations.idiomatic: Between father and son, what is hard for anyone to speak—yet Xin spoke of it. Was that not loyal earnestness?

sentences.zh: 今欲誅罪，不錄其心，臣愚竊以為過。」

translations.literal: Now if you wish to punish guilt without recording his intent, I foolishly think it a fault."
translations.idiomatic: Now if you wish to punish guilt without recording his intent, I foolishly think it a fault."

sentences.zh: 翌日，高祖召綱入，升御坐，謂曰：「今我有公，遂使刑罰不濫。

translations.literal: The next day Gaozu summoned Gang in, ascended the imperial seat, and said, "Now that I have you, punishments are not wantonly applied.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Gaozu summoned Gang in, ascended the imperial seat, and said, "Now that I have you, punishments are not wantonly applied.

sentences.zh: 元吉自惡，結怨於人。

translations.literal: Yuanji brings hatred on himself and makes enemies among men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji brings hatred on himself and makes enemies among men.

sentences.zh: 歆既曾以表聞，誕亦焉能禁制？

translations.literal: Xin had already reported by memorial; how could Yan have restrained him?
translations.idiomatic: Xin had already reported by memorial. How could Yan have restrained him?

sentences.zh: 皆非其罪也。」

translations.literal: Neither is guilty."
translations.idiomatic: Neither is guilty."

sentences.zh: 尋加授元吉侍中、襄州道行台尚書令、稷州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon Yuanji was further appointed Attendant-in-ordinary, Director of the Xiangzhou Circuit Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuanji was further appointed Attendant-in-ordinary, Director of the Xiangzhou Circuit Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，太宗征竇建德，留元吉與屈突通圍王世充於東都。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Taizong campaigned against Dou Jiande; Yuanji was left with Qu Tu Tong to besiege Wang Shichong at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Taizong campaigned against Dou Jiande. Yuanji was left with Qu Tu Tong to besiege Wang Shichong at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 世充出兵拒戰，元吉設伏擊破之，斬首八百級，生擒其大將樂仁昉、甲士千餘人。

translations.literal: Shichong sent troops out to resist; Yuanji set an ambush, routed them, took eight hundred heads, and captured alive his great general Yue Renfang and more than a thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent troops out to resist. Yuanji set an ambush, routed them, took eight hundred heads, and captured alive his great general Yue Renfang and more than a thousand armored soldiers.

sentences.zh: 世充平，拜司空，余官如故，加賜袞冕之服、前後部鼓吹樂二部、班劍二十人、黃金二千斤，與太宗各聽三爐鑄錢以自給。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified he was appointed Minister of Works; his other offices remained as before, and in addition he was granted robes of honor, two sets of front and rear guard music, twenty guards with swords, two thousand catties of gold, and he and Taizong were each permitted three mints to cast coin for their own supply.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong was pacified he was appointed Minister of Works. His other offices remained as before, and in addition he was granted robes of honor, two sets of front and rear guard music, twenty guards with swords, two thousand catties of gold, and he and Taizong were each permitted three mints to cast coin for their own supply.

sentences.zh: 六年，加授隰州總管。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was further appointed Inspector-General of Xi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was further appointed Inspector-General of Xi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及與建成連謀，各募壯士，多匿罪人。

translations.literal: When he joined Jiancheng in conspiracy they each recruited stalwart men and hid many criminals.
translations.idiomatic: When he joined Jiancheng in conspiracy they each recruited stalwart men and hid many criminals.

sentences.zh: 復內結宮掖，遞加稱譽，又厚賂中書令封倫以為黨助。

translations.literal: They also joined inwardly with the inner palace, heaping praise on one another, and richly bribed Director of the Department of State Affairs Feng Lun as a partisan ally.
translations.idiomatic: They also joined inwardly with the inner palace, heaping praise on one another, and richly bribed Director of the Department of State Affairs Feng Lun as a partisan ally.

sentences.zh: 由是高祖頗疏太宗而加愛元吉。

translations.literal: Hence Gaozu grew somewhat distant from Taizong and increased his love for Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Gaozu grew somewhat distant from Taizong and increased his love for Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗從高祖幸其第，元吉伏其護軍宇文寶於寢內，將以刺太宗。

translations.literal: When Taizong once followed Gaozu on a visit to his residence, Yuanji hid his Protector of the Army Yuwen Bao in the sleeping quarters intending to stab Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong once followed Gaozu on a visit to his residence, Yuanji hid his Protector of the Army Yuwen Bao in the sleeping quarters intending to stab Taizong.

sentences.zh: 建成恐事不果而止之，元吉慍曰：「為兄計耳，於我何害！」

translations.literal: Jiancheng feared the affair would not succeed and stopped him; Yuanji said angrily, "I am scheming for my elder brother—what harm is it to me!
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng feared the affair would not succeed and stopped him. Yuanji said angrily, "I am scheming for my elder brother—what harm is it to me!

sentences.zh: 九年，轉左衛大將軍，尋進位司徒、兼侍中，并州大都督、隰州都督、稷州刺史並如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Grand General of the Left Guard, and soon advanced to Minister of Education, concurrently Attendant-in-ordinary; his posts as Grand Commander of Bingzhou, Inspector-General of Xi, and Inspector of Jizhou remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to Grand General of the Left Guard, and soon advanced to Minister of Education, concurrently Attendant-in-ordinary. His posts as Grand Commander of Bingzhou, Inspector-General of Xi, and Inspector of Jizhou remained as before.

sentences.zh: 高祖將避暑太和宮，二王當從，元吉謂建成曰：「待至宮所，當興精兵襲取之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was about to take the summer retreat at Taihe Palace; the two princes were to accompany him. Yuanji said to Jiancheng, "When we reach the palace grounds we should raise elite troops and seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was about to take the summer retreat at Taihe Palace. The two princes were to accompany him. Yuanji said to Jiancheng, "When we reach the palace grounds we should raise elite troops and seize him.

sentences.zh: 置土窟中，唯開一孔以通飲食耳。」

translations.literal: Place him in an earthen pit with only one opening for food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Place him in an earthen pit with only one opening for food and drink.

sentences.zh: 會突厥郁射設屯軍河南，入圍烏城。

translations.literal: Just then the Turk Yugu She led troops south of the river and entered to besiege Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Turk Yugu She led troops south of the river and entered to besiege Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 建成乃薦元吉代太宗督軍北討，仍令秦府驍將秦叔寶、尉遲敬德、程知節、段志玄等並與同行。

translations.literal: Jiancheng then recommended Yuanji to replace Taizong in commanding the northern campaign, and ordered the Qin establishment's fierce generals Qin Shubao, Yuchi Jingde, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, and others to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng then recommended Yuanji to replace Taizong in commanding the northern campaign, and ordered the Qin establishment's fierce generals Qin Shubao, Yuchi Jingde, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, and others to go with him.

sentences.zh: 又追秦府兵帳，簡閱驍勇，將奪太宗兵以益其府。

translations.literal: He also pursued the Qin establishment's military rolls, selecting the fierce and brave, intending to seize Taizong's troops to augment his own establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He also pursued the Qin establishment's military rolls, selecting the fierce and brave, intending to seize Taizong's troops to augment his own establishment.

sentences.zh: 又譖杜如晦、房玄齡，逐令歸第。

translations.literal: He also slandered Du Ruhui and Fang Xuanling and had them sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He also slandered Du Ruhui and Fang Xuanling and had them sent home.

sentences.zh: 高祖知其謀而不制。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew their plot but did not restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu knew their plot but did not restrain it.

sentences.zh: 元吉因密請加害太宗，高祖曰：「是有定四海之功，罪跡未見，一旦欲殺，何以為辭？」

translations.literal: Yuanji then secretly requested that Taizong be killed; Gaozu said, "He has the merit of settling the four seas; his guilt is not yet seen—if you wish to kill him suddenly, what pretext will you have?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji then secretly requested that Taizong be killed. Gaozu said, "He has the merit of settling the four seas. His guilt is not yet seen—if you wish to kill him suddenly, what pretext will you have?"

sentences.zh: 元吉曰：「秦王常違詔敕，初平東都之日，偃蹇顧望，不急還京，分散錢帛，以樹私惠。

translations.literal: Yuanji said, "The Prince of Qin constantly disobeys edicts and instructions. When the eastern capital was first pacified he was arrogant and looked about, slow to return to the capital, and scattered money and silk to win private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, "The Prince of Qin constantly disobeys edicts and instructions. When the eastern capital was first pacified he was arrogant and looked about, slow to return to the capital, and scattered money and silk to win private favor.

sentences.zh: 違戾如此，豈非反逆？

translations.literal: Such defiance as this—is it not rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Such defiance as this—is it not rebellion?

sentences.zh: 但須速殺，何患無辭！」

translations.literal: One need only kill him quickly—why worry about lacking a pretext!"
translations.idiomatic: One need only kill him quickly—why worry about lacking a pretext!"

sentences.zh: 高祖不對，元吉遂退。

translations.literal: Gaozu did not reply; Yuanji then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu did not reply. Yuanji then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 建成謂元吉曰：「既得秦王精兵，統數萬之眾，吾與秦王至昆明池，於彼宴別，令壯士拉之於幕下，因雲暴卒，主上諒無不信。

translations.literal: Jiancheng said to Yuanji, "Now that we have obtained the Prince of Qin's elite troops and command tens of thousands of men, I and the Prince of Qin will go to Kunming Pool and there take leave at a banquet; let stalwart men drag him down behind the curtain and say he died suddenly—the sovereign will surely believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng said to Yuanji, "Now that we have obtained the Prince of Qin's elite troops and command tens of thousands of men, I and the Prince of Qin will go to Kunming Pool and there take leave at a banquet. Let stalwart men drag him down behind the curtain and say he died suddenly—the sovereign will surely believe it.

sentences.zh: 吾當使人進說，令付吾國務。

translations.literal: I will have men advance and persuade him to entrust state affairs to me.
translations.idiomatic: I will have men advance and persuade him to entrust state affairs to me.

sentences.zh: 正位已後，以汝為太弟。

translations.literal: Once I take the proper position I will make you Grand Younger Brother.
translations.idiomatic: Once I take the proper position I will make you Grand Younger Brother.

sentences.zh: 敬德等既入汝手，一時坑之，孰敢不服？」

translations.literal: Once Jingde and the others are in your hands, bury them all at once—who will dare not submit?
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingde and the others are in your hands, bury them all at once—who will dare not submit?

sentences.zh: 率更丞王晊聞其謀，密告太宗。

translations.literal: Court Director Wang Zhi heard their plot and secretly informed Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Court Director Wang Zhi heard their plot and secretly informed Taizong.

sentences.zh: 太宗召府僚以告之，皆曰：「大王若不正斷，社稷非唐所有。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned his establishment officials and told them; all said, "Great Prince, if you do not decide rightly, the altars of state will not belong to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned his establishment officials and told them. All said, "Great Prince, if you do not decide rightly, the altars of state will not belong to Tang.

sentences.zh: 若使建成、元吉肆其毒心，群小得志，元吉狼戾，終亦不事其兄。

translations.literal: If you let Jiancheng and Yuanji unleash their poison, petty men will have their way; Yuanji is fierce and cruel and in the end will not serve his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: If you let Jiancheng and Yuanji unleash their poison, petty men will have their way. Yuanji is fierce and cruel and in the end will not serve his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 往者護軍薛寶上齊王符籙云：『元吉合成唐字。』

translations.literal: Formerly Protector of the Army Xue Bao presented to the Prince of Qi a talisman slip saying, 'Yuanji completes the character for Tang.'
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Protector of the Army Xue Bao presented to the Prince of Qi a talisman slip saying, 'Yuanji completes the character for Tang.'

sentences.zh: 齊王得之喜曰：『但除秦王，取東宮如反掌耳。』

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, obtaining it, said with joy, 'Once the Prince of Qin is removed, taking the Eastern Palace will be like turning one's palm.'
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi, obtaining it, said with joy, 'Once the Prince of Qin is removed, taking the Eastern Palace will be like turning one's palm.'

sentences.zh: 為亂未成，預懷相奪。

translations.literal: Before the rebellion had even succeeded he already harbored designs to seize it from his brother.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rebellion had even succeeded he already harbored designs to seize it from his brother.

sentences.zh: 以大王之威，襲二人如拾地芥。」

translations.literal: With your Great Prince's prestige, to strike down the two of them would be like picking up dust from the ground."
translations.idiomatic: With your Great Prince's prestige, to strike down the two of them would be like picking up dust from the ground."

sentences.zh: 太宗遲疑未決，眾又曰：「大王以舜為何如人也？」

translations.literal: Taizong hesitated and had not decided; the crowd again said, "Great Prince, what sort of man do you take Shun to be?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong hesitated and had not decided. The crowd again said, "Great Prince, what sort of man do you take Shun to be?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「浚哲文明，溫恭允塞，為子孝，為君聖，焉可議之乎？」

translations.literal: He said, "Deeply wise and civilly accomplished, warm and respectful and truly sincere—as a son filial, as a ruler sage—how can he be discussed?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Deeply wise and civilly accomplished, warm and respectful and truly sincere—as a son filial, as a ruler sage—how can he be discussed?"

sentences.zh: 府僚曰：「向使舜浚井不出，自同魚鱉之斃，焉得為孝子乎？

translations.literal: If in former times Shun, when dredging a well, had not come out, he would himself have perished like fish and turtles—how then could he have been a filial son?
translations.idiomatic: Had Shun never climbed out of that well, he would have drowned like any fish or turtle—hardly the stuff of filial legend.

sentences.zh: 涂廩不下，便成煨燼之餘，焉得為聖君乎？

translations.literal: If Yu had not come down from the granary roof, he would straightway have become the remnant of smoldering ashes—how then could he have been a sage ruler?
translations.idiomatic: Had Yu failed to escape the burning granary, he would have been nothing but charred ruin—scarcely a model for sage kingship.

sentences.zh: 小杖受，大杖避，良有以也。」

translations.literal: To accept the small staff and to avoid the large staff—there is truly reason in this.
translations.idiomatic: Endure the light rod, flee the heavy one—there is wisdom in that ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 太宗於是定計誅建成及元吉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taizong settled on a plan to execute Jiancheng and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: At that Taizong resolved to kill Jiancheng and Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 元吉死時年二十四。

translations.literal: When Yuanji died, he was twenty-four years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was twenty-four when he was killed.

sentences.zh: 有五子：梁郡王承業、漁陽王承鸞、普安王承獎、江夏王承裕、義陽王承度，並坐誅。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Liang Commandery Prince Chengye, Yuyang Prince Chengluan, Pu'an Prince Chengjian, Jiangxia Prince Chengyu, and Yiyang Prince Chengnu—all were executed for complicity.
translations.idiomatic: His five sons—Chengye, Prince of Liang Commandery; Chengluan, Prince of Yuyang; Chengjian, Prince of Pu'an; Chengyu, Prince of Jiangxia; and Chengnu, Prince of Yiyang—were all put to death as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 尋詔絕建成、元吉屬籍。

translations.literal: Soon an edict was issued expunging Jiancheng and Yuanji from the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict struck Jiancheng and Yuanji from the imperial genealogy.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐祚，追封元吉為海陵郡王，謚曰剌，以禮改葬。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Yuanji as Prince of Hailing Commandery, with the posthumous title Li (Censorious), and had him reburied according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong took the throne, he posthumously made Yuanji Prince of Hailing Commandery, gave him the posthumous name Li, and reinterred him with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十六年，又追封巢王，謚如故，復以曹王明為元吉後。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan, he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Chao, the posthumous title remaining as before, and Cao Prince Li Ming was again made Yuanji's heir.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 16 Yuanji was raised posthumously to Prince of Chao, his censorious epithet unchanged, and Li Ming, Prince of Cao, was once more appointed his successor.

sentences.zh: 楚王智雲

translations.literal: Prince of Chu, Zhiyun
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyun, Prince of Chu

sentences.zh: 荊王元景

translations.literal: Prince of Jing, Yuanjing
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing, Prince of Jing

sentences.zh: 荊王元景，高祖第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jing, Yuanjing, was the sixth son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing, Prince of Jing, was Gaozu's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，封為趙王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 3: he received the title Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 八年，授安州都督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was appointed Area Commander of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he became Area Commander of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷遷雍州牧、右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he successively served as Governor of Yongzhou and General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he held the posts of Yongzhou Governor and General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard in turn.

sentences.zh: 十年，徙封荊王，授荊州都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, his fief was changed to Prince of Jing, and he was appointed Area Commander of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Year ten: he was transferred to Prince of Jing and made Area Commander of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十一年，定制元景等為代襲刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, regulations were established making Yuanjing and others hereditary prefects.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven a system was decreed whereby Yuanjing and the other princes would hold their prefectures in perpetual succession.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: The edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared:

sentences.zh: 皇王受命，步驟之跡以殊；

translations.literal: When sovereign kings receive the Mandate, the steps of their ascent differ;
translations.idiomatic: Kings who take Heaven's charge walk different paths to power;

sentences.zh: 經籍所紀，質文之道匪一。

translations.literal: what the classics record shows that the way of substance and ornament is not one.
translations.idiomatic: yet the classics show that no single formula governs how rule should be shaped in letter and spirit.

sentences.zh: 雖治亂不同，損益或異，至於設官司以制海內，建籓屏以輔王室，莫不明其典章，義存於致治；

translations.literal: Though order and disorder differ and gains and losses vary, as for establishing offices to govern the realm within the seas and erecting screen-walls to assist the royal house—none fail to clarify their statutes, the meaning lying in achieving good governance;
translations.idiomatic: Whether times are turbulent or calm, reforms wax or wane, every age that sets officials over the empire and raises feudal shields for the throne has codified its institutions to the end of good order;

sentences.zh: 崇其賢戚，志在於無疆。

translations.literal: to honor worthy kinsmen is a purpose whose reach knows no bounds.
translations.idiomatic: and to exalt royal kin is to aim at a dynasty without limit.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，丕承鴻緒，寅畏三靈，憂勤百姓，考明哲之餘論，求經邦之長策。

translations.literal: I, being dull and ignorant, greatly inherit the vast succession, stand in awe before the Three Powers, and toil in concern for the hundred surnames, examining the remaining discourse of the wise and seeking long policies for governing the state.
