translations.idiomatic: Humbly I have taken up the great legacy, tremble before Heaven, Earth, and the spirits, and labor for the people—studying sage counsel and searching out enduring ways to govern.

sentences.zh: 帝業之重，獨任難以成務；

translations.literal: The weight of the imperial enterprise—alone to bear it is hard to accomplish the task;
translations.idiomatic: The burden of empire is too heavy for one man alone;

sentences.zh: 天下之曠，因人易以獲安。

translations.literal: the vastness of the realm—through men it is easy to obtain peace.
translations.idiomatic: the breadth of the realm finds its peace only through the right men.

sentences.zh: 然則侯伯肇於自昔，州郡始於中代，聖賢異術，沿革隨時，復古則義難頓從，尋今則事不盡理。

translations.literal: Thus marquis-lords arose from antiquity and prefectures and commanderies began in the middle ages; sages and worthies used different methods, and change followed the times— to restore the ancient would make obedience to principle suddenly difficult, while to follow the present would not exhaust reason in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Marquisates date to antiquity and commandery rule to the middle kingdoms; sages chose different tools and institutions shifted with the age. Blind restoration would jar against necessity, yet clinging only to the present would fall short of principle.

sentences.zh: 遂規模周、漢，斟酌曹、馬，采按部之嘉名，參建侯之舊制，共治之職重矣，分土之實存焉。

translations.literal: Accordingly I took Zhou and Han as models, weighed Cao and Sima, selected the fine names of territorial divisions, and consulted the old system of establishing feudatories— the office of shared governance grows weighty, and the reality of granting land remains.
translations.idiomatic: So I looked to Zhou and Han, weighed the precedents of Cao Wei and the Sima Jin, drew on honored regional titles, and revived the old pattern of enfeoffment—making shared rule a weighty charge while keeping the substance of granted domains.

sentences.zh: 已有制書，陳其至理。

translations.literal: An edict of regulation has already been issued, setting forth its utmost principle.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations have already been promulgated, stating the full rationale.

sentences.zh: 繼世垂範，貽厥後昆；

translations.literal: To pass the age to posterity and bequeath a model to later generations;
translations.idiomatic: May this endure from age to age, a standard for those who come after;

sentences.zh: 維城作固，同符前烈。

translations.literal: to make the wall of the realm firm accords with former achievements.
translations.idiomatic: and may it buttress the realm as the great founders did of old.

sentences.zh: 荊州都督荊王元景、梁州都督漢王元昌、徐州都督徐王元禮、潞州都督韓王元嘉、遂州都督彭王元則、鄭州刺史鄭王元懿、絳州刺史霍王元軌、虢州刺史虢王鳳、豫州刺史道王元慶、鄧州刺史鄧王元裕、壽州刺史舒王元名、幽州都督燕王靈夔、蘇州刺史許王元祥、安州都督吳王恪、相州都督魏王泰、齊州都督齊王裕、益州都督蜀王愔、襄州刺史蔣王惲、揚州都督越王貞、并州都督晉王某、秦州都督紀王慎等，或地居旦、奭，夙聞《詩》、《禮》；

translations.literal: Area Commander of Jingzhou, Prince of Jing Yuanjing; Area Commander of Liangzhou, Prince of Han Yuan Chang; Area Commander of Xuzhou, Prince of Xu Yuanli; Area Commander of Luzhou, Prince of Han Yuanjia; Area Commander of Suizhou, Prince of Peng Yuanze; Prefect of Zhengzhou, Prince of Zheng Yuanyi; Prefect of Jiangzhou, Prince of Huo Yuangui; Prefect of Guozhou, Prince of Guo Feng; Prefect of Yuzhou, Prince of Dao Yuanqing; Prefect of Dengzhou, Prince of Deng Yuanyu; Prefect of Shouzhou, Prince of Shu Yuanming; Area Commander of Youzhou, Prince of Yan Lingkui; Prefect of Suzhou, Prince of Xu Yuanxiang; Area Commander of Anzhou, Prince of Wu Ké; Area Commander of Xiangzhou, Prince of Wei Yuantai; Area Commander of Qizhou, Prince of Qi Yu; Area Commander of Yizhou, Prince of Shu Yuanyin; Prefect of Xiangzhou, Prince of Jiang Yun; Area Commander of Yangzhou, Prince of Yue Zhen; Area Commander of Bingzhou, a certain Prince of Jin; Area Commander of Qinzhou, Prince of Ji Shen, and others—some occupy lands like those of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, and from youth have heard the Odes and Rites;
translations.idiomatic: Among them are Jingzhou Area Commander Yuanjing, Prince of Jing; Liangzhou Area Commander Yuanchang, Prince of Han; Xuzhou Area Commander Yuanli, Prince of Xu; Luzhou Area Commander Yuanjia, Prince of Han; Suizhou Area Commander Yuanze, Prince of Peng; Zhengzhou Prefect Yuanyi, Prince of Zheng; Jiangzhou Prefect Yuangui, Prince of Huo; Guozhou Prefect Feng, Prince of Guo; Yuzhou Prefect Yuanqing, Prince of Dao; Dengzhou Prefect Yuanyu, Prince of Deng; Shouzhou Prefect Yuanming, Prince of Shu; Youzhou Area Commander Lingkui, Prince of Yan; Suzhou Prefect Yuanxiang, Prince of Xu; Anzhou Area Commander Ké, Prince of Wu; Xiangzhou Area Commander Yuantai, Prince of Wei; Qizhou Area Commander Yu, Prince of Qi; Yizhou Area Commander Yuanyin, Prince of Shu; Xiang Prefecture Prefect Yun, Prince of Jiang; Yangzhou Area Commander Zhen, Prince of Yue; Bingzhou Area Commander, a Prince of Jin [name omitted]; Qinzhou Area Commander Shen, Prince of Ji—some raised in domains worthy of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, steeped since boyhood in the Odes and Rites;

sentences.zh: 或望及間、平，早稱才藝，並爵隆土宇，寵兼車服。

translations.literal: some whose repute reaches that of Jian and Ping, who early were acclaimed for talent and skill—all with lofty rank over lands, favor joined to chariots and robes.
translations.idiomatic: others whose fame rivals the great exemplars Jian and Ping, praised early for ability and arts—all ennobled over broad fiefs, honored with carriages and vestments.

sentences.zh: 誠孝之心，無忘於造次；

translations.literal: The heart of sincere filial piety is not forgotten even in haste;
translations.idiomatic: Filial devotion they never set aside, even in hurried moments;

sentences.zh: 風政之舉，克著於期月。

translations.literal: their conduct in governance and policy has been clearly established within a month's time.
translations.idiomatic: and their governance has already shown itself within a single month.

sentences.zh: 宜冠恆冊，祚以休命。

translations.literal: They should be crowned in the eternal registers and invested with blessings and commands.
translations.idiomatic: Let them stand foremost in the everlasting rolls and receive this gracious appointment.

sentences.zh: 其所任刺史，咸令子孫代代承襲。

translations.literal: The prefectural posts they hold—all are commanded that sons and grandsons shall inherit them generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures they now hold shall pass from son to grandson, generation upon generation.

sentences.zh: 尋又罷代襲之制。

translations.literal: Before long the system of hereditary succession was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the hereditary prefect system was revoked.

sentences.zh: 元景久之轉鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long interval Yuanjing was transferred to Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In time Yuanjing was moved to the post of Prefect of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，進位司徒，加實封通前滿一千五百戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, Yuanjing was promoted to Grand Tutor, and his actual fief households were increased to a total of one thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's accession he rose to Grand Tutor, his income fief reaching fifteen hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，坐與房遺愛謀反賜死，國除。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui, for plotting rebellion with Fang Yi'ai he was sentenced to death and his fief abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghui 4: convicted of treason with Fang Yi'ai, he was executed and his princedom extinguished.

sentences.zh: 後追封沉黎王，備禮改葬。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chenli, and reburied with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously made Prince of Chenli and given a proper reburial.

sentences.zh: 以渤海王奉慈子長沙為嗣，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: Changsha, son of Bohai Prince Fengci, was made heir, but the rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Fengci's son Changsha was appointed successor, though reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追復爵土，並封其孫逖為嗣荊王，尋薨，國除。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, his title and lands were restored, and his grandson Ti was enfeoffed as successor Prince of Jing; soon after he died, and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shenlong his honors were restored and his grandson Ti made Prince of Jing in succession; Ti soon died and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 漢王元昌

translations.literal: Prince of Han, Yuanchang
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang, Prince of Han

sentences.zh: 漢王元昌，高祖第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Han, Yuanchang, was the seventh son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang, Prince of Han, was Gaozu's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善隸書。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled at clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied eagerly and wrote a fine clerical hand.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，封為魯王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 3: he was created Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，授華州刺史，轉梁州都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan, he was appointed Prefect of Huazhou and then transferred to Area Commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 5 brought him the Huazhou prefecture and then the Liangzhou command.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封漢王。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, his title was changed to Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten his fief became Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 元昌在州，頗違憲法，太宗手敕責之。

translations.literal: While Yuanchang was in his province, he greatly violated the statutes; Taizong personally wrote an edict rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang's rule in Liangzhou flouted the law, and Taizong sent a personal rebuke.

sentences.zh: 初不自咎，更懷怨望。

translations.literal: At first he did not blame himself, but instead harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He showed no remorse at first, only growing resentful.

sentences.zh: 知太子承乾嫉魏王泰之寵，乃相附托，圖為不軌。

translations.literal: Knowing that the Crown Prince Chenggan envied Prince of Wei Yuantai's favor, he attached himself to Chenggan and plotted unlawful designs.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Crown Prince Chenggan resented Yuantai, Prince of Wei, for their father's favor, he joined the heir and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十六年，元昌來朝京師，承乾頻召入東宮夜宿，因謂承乾曰：「願陛下早為天子。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when Yuanchang came to court at the capital, Chenggan repeatedly summoned him to stay overnight in the Eastern Palace, and Yuanchang said to Chenggan: "I hope Your Majesty will soon become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen Yuanchang arrived at court; Chenggan often had him sleep in the Eastern Palace and said, "May Your Majesty take the throne soon.

sentences.zh: 近見御側，有一宮人，善彈琵琶，事平之後，當望垂賜。」

translations.literal: Recently I saw at Your Majesty's side a palace woman skilled at playing the pipa—when the affair is settled, I hope she may be granted to me.
translations.idiomatic: I lately noticed a pipa player in your father's train—when all is settled, I trust you will give her to me.

sentences.zh: 承乾許諾。

translations.literal: Chenggan promised.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 又刻臂出血，以帛拭之，燒作灰，和酒同飲，共為信誓，潛伺間隙。

translations.literal: They further carved their arms to draw blood, wiped it with silk, burned the cloth to ash, mixed it with wine, and drank together, making a secret oath while watching for an opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: They cut their arms, caught the blood on silk, burned the cloth to ash, mixed it with wine, and drank as one—a blood oath while they waited for their chance.

sentences.zh: 十七年，事發，太宗弗忍加誅，特敕免死。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when the affair came to light, Taizong could not bear to put him to death and specially ordered that his life be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Year seventeen: the plot exposed, Taizong could not bring himself to execute him and specially granted life.

sentences.zh: 大臣高士廉、李世勣等奏言：「王者以四海為家，以萬姓為子，公行天下，情無獨親。

translations.literal: The ministers Gao Shilian, Li Shiji, and others memorialized, saying: "A king takes the four seas as his home and the myriad surnames as his children; in public conduct throughout the realm, affection cannot be reserved for kin alone.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Gao Shilian and Li Shiji submitted: "A true king treats the realm as home and all people as his children; in ruling the world, private affection must not outweigh public duty.

sentences.zh: 元昌苞藏凶惡，圖謀逆亂，觀其指趣，察其心府，罪深燕旦，釁甚楚英。

translations.literal: Yuanchang harbored fierce wickedness and plotted rebellion and disorder; observing his aim and examining his heart, his crime is deeper than that of Prince Dan of Yan, his offense greater than that of Prince Ying of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang concealed vicious intent and plotted revolt; judged by aim and heart, his guilt surpasses Prince Dan of Yan's, his treason worse than Prince Ying of Chu's.

sentences.zh: 天地之所不容，人臣之所切齒，五刑不足申其罰，九死無以當其愆。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth cannot contain him; ministers grind their teeth at him—the five punishments are insufficient to declare his penalty, and nine deaths cannot match his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth would reject such a man; every loyal minister gnashes his teeth—the five punishments are too light, nine deaths too few.

sentences.zh: 而陛下情屈至公，恩加梟獍，欲開疏網，漏此鯨鯢。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty's feeling bends to utmost fairness, your grace extends even to the owl and the jackal, wishing to open a loose net and let slip this whale and crocodile.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty's justice wavers toward mercy, extending grace even to monsters, as if to cast a wide net and release this leviathan.

sentences.zh: 臣等有司，期不奉制，伏願敦師憲典，誅此凶慝。

translations.literal: We, your officials, expect that we cannot obey such an order; we humbly hope you will uphold the teacher's canonical law and execute this wicked villain.
translations.idiomatic: We your servants cannot in conscience obey; we beg you uphold the law and put this villain to death.

sentences.zh: 順群臣之願，奪鷹鸇之心，則吳、楚七君，不幽嘆於往漢；

translations.literal: If you follow the wish of the multitude of ministers and remove the heart of the hawk and the falcon, then the seven lords of Wu and Chu will not sigh in obscurity under the former Han;
translations.idiomatic: Grant the court's plea, steel your heart as a ruler must, and the seven princes of Wu and Chu will not groan unavenged under the Han;

sentences.zh: 管、蔡二叔，不沉恨於有周。」

translations.literal: nor will the two uncles Guan and Cai lie buried in resentment under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: nor Guan and Cai, the two uncles of Zhou, rest embittered beneath the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗事不獲已，乃賜元昌自盡於家，妻子籍沒，國除。

translations.literal: Taizong, the matter being unavoidable, then ordered Yuanchang to take his own life at home; his wife and children were registered as slaves and the fief abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse, Taizong commanded Yuanchang to kill himself at home; his family was confiscated and the princedom ended.

sentences.zh: 酆王元亨

translations.literal: Prince of Feng, Yuanheng
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng, Prince of Feng

sentences.zh: 酆王元亨，高祖第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Feng, Yuanheng, was the eighth son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng, Prince of Feng, was Gaozu's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 武德三年受封。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude he received his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Wude 3.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，授散騎常侍，拜金州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, he was appointed Attendant Cavalier and invested as Prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 2: he became Attendant Cavalier and Prefect of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及之籓，太宗以其幼小，甚思之，中路賜以金盞，遣使為之設宴。

translations.literal: When he reached his fief, Taizong, because he was still very young, missed him greatly; midway he bestowed a golden cup upon him and sent an envoy to hold a feast on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: On the road to his fief the boy prince was still so young that Taizong missed him sorely; the emperor sent ahead a golden goblet and an envoy to feast him on the way.

sentences.zh: 六年薨，無子，國除。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; he had no son, and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year six without heirs, and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 周王元方

translations.literal: Prince of Zhou, Yuanfang
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang, Prince of Zhou

sentences.zh: 周王元方，高祖第九子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhou, Yuanfang, was the ninth son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang, Prince of Zhou, was Gaozu's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 武德四年受封。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude he received his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He received his title in Wude 4.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，授散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, he was appointed Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 2: he was made Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 三年薨，贈左光祿大夫，無子，國除。

translations.literal: In the third year he died; he was posthumously given the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, had no son, and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year three, was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, left no son, and the fief ended.

sentences.zh: 徐王元禮

translations.literal: Prince of Xu, Yuanli
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli, Prince of Xu

sentences.zh: 徐王元禮，高祖第十子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xu, Yuanli, was the tenth son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli, Prince of Xu, was Gaozu's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 少恭謹，善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he was respectful and careful, and skilled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was modest and diligent as a youth, and excelled at riding and shooting.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，封鄭王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: he became Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，賜實封七百戶，授鄭州刺史，徙封徐王，遷徐州都督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, he was granted an actual fief of seven hundred households, appointed Prefect of Zhengzhou, transferred to Prince of Xu, and moved to Area Commander of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 6: he received seven hundred income households, took Zhengzhou, was transferred to Prince of Xu, and became Xuzhou Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 十七年，轉絳州刺史，以善政聞，太宗降璽書勞勉，賜以錦彩。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was transferred to Prefect of Jiangzhou; his good governance became known, and Taizong sent an imperial letter of commendation and bestowed brocades.
translations.idiomatic: Year seventeen he moved to Jiang Prefecture; his able rule won notice, and Taizong sent a sealed letter of praise with silks.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, his actual fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three his income fief grew by a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，加授司徒，兼潞州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui, he was further appointed Grand Tutor and concurrently Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghui 4: he was also made Grand Tutor and Prefect of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸亨三年薨，贈太尉、冀州大都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianheng he died; he was posthumously given the titles of Grand Commandant and Area Commander-in-Chief of Jizhou, and buried alongside Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianheng 3, was posthumously named Grand Commandant and Jizhou Area Commander-in-Chief, and interred at Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 淮南王茂嗣

translations.literal: Huainan Prince Maosi
translations.idiomatic: Maosi, Prince of Huainan

sentences.zh: 韓王元嘉

translations.literal: Prince of Han, Yuanjia
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia, Prince of Han

sentences.zh: 韓王元嘉，高祖第十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Han, Yuanjia, was the eleventh son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia, Prince of Han, was Gaozu's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 母宇文昭儀，隋左武衛大將軍述之女也。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Zhao of the Yuwen clan, daughter of Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zhao of Yuwen, was daughter of Yuwen Shu, Sui's General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 早有寵於高祖，高祖初即位，便欲立為皇后，固辭不受。

translations.literal: She had long enjoyed Gaozu's favor; when Gaozu first ascended the throne, he wished to make her empress, but she firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: She had long been Gaozu's favorite; when he first took the throne he wished to make her empress, but she steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 元嘉少以母寵，特為高祖所愛，自登極晚生皇子，無及之者。

translations.literal: Yuanjia, in youth favored through his mother, was especially loved by Gaozu; among the princes born after Gaozu's late accession, none matched him.
translations.idiomatic: Favored through his mother, Yuanjia was especially dear to Gaozu—none of the sons born after the founding matched his place in the emperor's heart.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，封宋王，徙封徐王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Song, then transferred to Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4: he was made Prince of Song, then Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，賜實封七百戶，授潞州刺史，時年十五。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, he was granted an actual fief of seven hundred households and appointed Prefect of Luzhou; at the time he was fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 6: seven hundred income households and the Lu Prefecture post came to him at age fifteen.

sentences.zh: 在州聞太妃有疾，便涕泣不食。

translations.literal: While in his province, when he heard that the Princess Dowager was ill, he wept and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in Lu, he learned his mother was ill and wept until he would not eat.

sentences.zh: 及京師發喪，哀毀過禮，太宗嗟其至性，屢慰勉之。

translations.literal: When mourning was raised in the capital, his grief exceeded the rites; Taizong sighed at his utmost nature and repeatedly comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: At her funeral in the capital his grief exceeded propriety; Taizong marveled at such filial depth and consoled him again and again.

sentences.zh: 九年，授右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed General of the Right Leading Army.
translations.idiomatic: Year nine: he became General of the Right Leading Army.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封韓王，授潞州都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, his title was changed to Prince of Han, and he was appointed Area Commander of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he was made Prince of Han and Luzhou Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, his actual fief was increased to one thousand households in total.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty-three brought his income fief to a full thousand households.

sentences.zh: 元嘉少好學，聚書至萬卷，又采碑文古蹟，多得異本。

translations.literal: Yuanjia from youth loved learning; he collected books to the number of ten thousand scrolls, and gathering inscriptions and ancient traces, he obtained many rare editions.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia loved books from boyhood, amassed ten thousand volumes, and by collecting stele texts and antiquities gathered many unusual editions.

sentences.zh: 閨門修整，有類寒素士大夫。

translations.literal: Within his household he maintained strict order, resembling a poor scholar-official family.
translations.idiomatic: His household was run with austere decorum, like that of a modest scholar's family.

sentences.zh: 與其弟靈夔甚相友愛，兄弟集見，如布衣之禮。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Lingkui he was deeply friendly and affectionate; when the brothers gathered and met, they observed the etiquette of commoners in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished an especially close bond with his brother Lingkui; whenever they met, the two brothers treated one another with the unpretentious courtesy of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 其修身潔己，內外如一，當代諸王莫能及者，唯霍王元軌抑其次焉。

translations.literal: In cultivating his person and keeping himself pure, he was one inside and out; among the princes of the age none could reach him — only Prince Yuangui of Huo was next.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was disciplined and consistent in public and private alike; of all the princes of their day, none matched him, with Prince Yuangui of Huo alone ranking second.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，元嘉轉澤州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Gaozong's reign, Yuanjia was transferred to Cizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the close of Emperor Gaozong's reign, Yuanjia was reassigned as prefect of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 及天后臨朝攝政，欲順物情，乃進授元嘉為太尉，定州刺史、霍王元軌為司徒，青州刺史、舒王元名為司空，隆州刺史、魯王靈夔為太子太師，蘇州刺史、越王貞為太子太傅，安州都督、紀王慎為太子太保，並外示尊崇，實無所綜理。

translations.literal: When the Heavenly Empress attended court and held regency, wishing to accord with popular sentiment, she then advanced and appointed Yuanjia as Grand Commandant; Prince Yuangui of Huo, prefect of Dingzhou, as Minister of Education; Prince Yuanming of Shu, prefect of Qingzhou, as Minister of Works; Prince Lingkui of Lu, prefect of Longzhou, as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Prince Zhen of Yue, prefect of Suzhou, as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; and Prince Shen of Ji, governor-general of Anzhou, as Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent — all outwardly showing honor, but in reality having nothing to administer.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, seeking to placate public opinion, she promoted Yuanjia to Grand Commandant; Prince Yuangui of Huo, prefect of Dingzhou, to Minister of Education; Prince Yuanming of Shu, prefect of Qingzhou, to Minister of Works; Prince Lingkui of Lu, prefect of Longzhou, to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Prince Zhen of Yue, prefect of Suzhou, to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; and Prince Shen of Ji, governor-general of Anzhou, to Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent — titles meant to honor them in appearance, though they carried no real administrative duties.

sentences.zh: 其後漸將誅戮宗室諸王不附己者，元嘉大懼，與其子通州刺史、黃公譔及越王貞父子謀起兵，於是皇宗國戚內外相連者甚廣。

translations.literal: Thereafter she gradually began to execute and kill among the imperial clansmen those princes who did not attach themselves to her. Yuanjia was greatly afraid, and with his son, Tongzhou prefect the Duke of Huang Fu, and Prince Zhen of Yue and his son plotted to raise troops. Thus among the imperial clan and royal kin, those connected within and without became very extensive.
translations.idiomatic: She then began systematically to eliminate princes of the imperial house who refused to align with her. Yuanjia was seized with terror and, together with his son Fu — prefect of Tongzhou and Duke of Huang — and Prince Zhen of Yue and his son, plotted an armed uprising. The conspiracy drew in a wide network of royal relatives and consanguineous allies.

sentences.zh: 遣使報貞及貞子琅邪王沖曰：「四面同來，事無不濟。」

translations.literal: He sent envoys to report to Zhen and Zhen's son, Prince Chong of Langye, saying: "If all four sides come together, the affair cannot fail."
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched messengers to Prince Zhen and his son Prince Chong of Langye with word that if forces converged from every quarter, the enterprise was sure to succeed.

sentences.zh: 沖與諸道計料未審而先發兵，倉卒唯貞應之，諸道莫有赴者，故其事不成。

translations.literal: Chong, together with the various routes, had not yet fully calculated the plan when he first raised troops. In haste only Zhen responded; of the various routes none came, and therefore the affair did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, however, mobilized before the allied provinces had settled their plans. In the rush only Prince Zhen answered the call; no other column marched, and the rebellion collapsed.

sentences.zh: 元嘉坐誅。

translations.literal: Yuanjia was executed on account of the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia was put to death for his part in the plot.

sentences.zh: 譔少以文才見知，諸王子中，與琅邪王沖為一時之秀，凡所交結皆當代名士。

translations.literal: Fu from youth was known for literary talent; among the princes' sons, he and Prince Chong of Langye were the outstanding talents of the age. All whom he befriended were famous scholars of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had won early renown for his literary gifts; among the sons of princes he and Prince Chong of Langye stood out as the finest minds of their generation, and his circle included the leading men of letters of the day.

sentences.zh: 時天下犯罪籍沒者甚眾，唯沖與譔父子書籍最多，皆文句詳定，秘閣所不及。

translations.literal: At the time throughout the realm those who committed crimes and had their property confiscated were very numerous; only Chong and Fu, father and son, had the most books — all with texts carefully settled, which the Secret Archive could not match.
translations.idiomatic: Confiscations of property from convicted offenders were widespread at the time, yet the libraries of Chong and of Fu and his father were the largest of all — their texts meticulously collated, surpassing even the holdings of the imperial Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追復元嘉爵土，並封其第五子訥為嗣韓王，官至員外祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, Yuanjia's title and fief were posthumously restored, and his fifth son Ne was enfeoffed as heir to the Prince of Han, reaching the office of supernumerary libationer.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening year of the Shenlong reign, Yuanjia's rank and domain were posthumously reinstated, and his fifth son Ne was created heir to the Han princedom, later serving as supernumerary libationer.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year of the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 元嘉長子訓，高祖時封潁川王，早卒。

translations.literal: Yuanjia's eldest son Xun, in Gaozu's time was enfeoffed as Prince of Yingchuan, and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia's eldest son Xun had been created Prince of Yingchuan under Gaozu but died young.

sentences.zh: 次子誼，封武陵王，官至濮州刺史。

translations.literal: The second son Yi was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling, and reached the office of Puzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Yi was created Prince of Wuling and rose to the post of prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元中，封訥子叔璇為嗣韓王、國子員外司業。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Ne's son Shuxuan was enfeoffed as heir Prince of Han and supernumerary vice-director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan period, Ne's son Shuxuan was made heir to the Han princedom and appointed supernumerary vice-director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 彭王元則

translations.literal: Prince of Peng, Yuanze
translations.idiomatic: Yuanze, Prince of Peng

sentences.zh: 彭王元則，高祖第十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yuanze of Peng was Gaozu's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanze of Peng was the twelfth son of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，封荊王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Wude era he was created Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，授豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he was appointed Yuzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Zhenguan era he was appointed prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封彭王，除遂州都督，尋坐章服奢僭免官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Prince of Peng, dismissed as Suizhou governor-general, and soon on account of extravagant and presumptuous insignia and dress was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his title was changed to Prince of Peng and he was made governor-general of Suizhou; he was soon stripped of his post for ostentatious and presumptuous dress and insignia.

sentences.zh: 十七年，拜澧州刺史，更折節勵行，頗著聲譽。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Lizhou prefect, further restraining his conduct and encouraging his behavior, and achieved considerable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed prefect of Lizhou, where he redoubled his self-discipline and won a notable reputation.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年薨，高宗為之廢朝三日，贈司徒、荊州都督，陪葬獻陵，謚曰思。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he died. Gaozong for him suspended court for three days, posthumously granted Minister of Education and Jingzhou governor-general, buried with Xian Mausoleum, posthumous title Si.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Yonghui era. Emperor Gaozong canceled court for three days in mourning, posthumously ennobled him as Minister of Education and governor-general of Jingzhou, had him interred at Xian Mausoleum, and gave him the posthumous name Si, "Reflective."

sentences.zh: 發引之日，高宗登望春宮望其靈車，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: On the day the funeral procession set out, Gaozong ascended Wangchun Palace to look upon his spirit carriage and wept with extreme grief.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the funeral cortege departed, Gaozong climbed to Wangchun Palace to watch the bier pass and wept with deep anguish.

sentences.zh: 無子，以霍王元軌子絢嗣，龍朔中封南昌王。

translations.literal: Having no son, Prince Yuangui of Huo's son Xuan was made heir; in the Longshuo era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, so Yuangui's son Xuan was adopted as his heir and, during the Longshuo era, was created Prince of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 子志暕，神龍初封嗣彭王。

translations.literal: His son Zhijian, at the beginning of Shenlong was enfeoffed as heir Prince of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhijian was created heir to the Peng princedom at the opening of the Shenlong reign.

sentences.zh: 景龍初，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jinglong he was given the additional title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jinglong era he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 開元中，宗正卿同正員，卒。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, supernumerary director of the Imperial Clan Court, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan period he served as supernumerary director of the Imperial Clan Court and later died.

sentences.zh: 鄭王元懿

translations.literal: Prince of Zheng, Yuanyi
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi, Prince of Zheng

sentences.zh: 鄭王元懿，高祖第十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yuanyi of Zheng was Gaozu's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanyi of Zheng was the thirteenth son of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 頗好學。

translations.literal: He rather loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was an avid student of the classics.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，封滕王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Teng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Wude era he was created Prince of Teng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，授兗州刺史，賜實封六百戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he was appointed Yanzhou prefect and granted six hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Zhenguan era he was made prefect of Yanzhou and granted a substantive fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封鄭王，歷鄭、潞二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Prince of Zheng, and successively served as Zheng and Lu prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his title was changed to Prince of Zheng, and he served in turn as prefect of Zheng and Lu.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 總章中，累授絳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Zongzhang era he was repeatedly appointed Jiangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zongzhang period he was appointed prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 數斷大獄，甚有平允之譽。

translations.literal: He several times decided major cases and had a considerable reputation for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over numerous major trials and earned wide praise for equitable judgments.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘉之，降璽書褒美，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: Gaozong commended him, sent down an imperial-seal letter praising him, and bestowed three hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong applauded his service, issued an edict under the imperial seal commending him, and granted three hundred rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 咸亨四年薨，贈司徒、荊州大都督，謚曰惠，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianheng he died, posthumously granted Minister of Education and Jingzhou governor-general, posthumous title Hui, buried with Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Xianheng era and was posthumously ennobled as Minister of Education and governor-general of Jingzhou, given the posthumous name Hui, "Benevolent," and interred at Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 子璥，上元初，封為嗣鄭王，官至鄂州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Jing, at the beginning of Shangyuan, was enfeoffed as heir Prince of Zheng, and reached the office of Ezhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing was created heir to the Zheng princedom at the opening of the Shangyuan era and rose to prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，又封璥嫡子希言為嗣鄭王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Jing's eldest legitimate son Xiyan was again enfeoffed as heir Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenlong reign, Jing's eldest legitimate son Xiyan was likewise created heir to the Zheng princedom.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年，嗣鄭王希言等共一十四人，並加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jinglong, heir Prince of Zheng Xiyan and others, fourteen in all, were all given the additional title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jinglong era, Xiyan, heir to the Zheng princedom, and thirteen others were all promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 開元中，右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Right General of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan period he served as Right General of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，再為太子詹事同正員，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, again served as supernumerary steward of the Heir Apparent, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was again appointed supernumerary steward of the Heir Apparent and later died.

sentences.zh: 霍王元軌

translations.literal: Prince of Huo, Yuangui
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui, Prince of Huo

sentences.zh: 霍王元軌，高祖第十四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yuangui of Huo was Gaozu's fourteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuangui of Huo was the fourteenth son of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 少多才藝，高祖甚奇之。

translations.literal: From youth he had many talents and arts; Gaozu greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he displayed wide-ranging talents, and Gaozu took a keen interest in him.

sentences.zh: 武德六年，封蜀王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Wude era he was created Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 八年，徙封吳王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his title was changed to Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，太宗嘗問群臣曰：「朕子弟孰賢？」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Taizong once asked the assembled ministers, saying: "Among my sons and younger brothers, who is worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, Emperor Taizong once asked his ministers, "Which of my sons and brothers is the most capable?

sentences.zh: 侍中魏徵對曰：「臣愚闇，不盡知其能。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Wei Zheng replied, saying: "Your servant is dull and dark, and does not fully know their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Wei Zheng answered, "I am too dull to judge them all with certainty.

sentences.zh: 唯吳王數與臣言，未嘗不自失。」

translations.literal: Only the Prince of Wu has several times spoken with me, and I have never failed to lose myself."
translations.idiomatic: But whenever I have spoken with the Prince of Wu, I have always found myself at a loss before him."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕亦器之，卿以為前代誰比？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I too value him. To whom of former ages do you compare him?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I hold him in high regard as well. To whom in past ages would you compare him?"

sentences.zh: 征曰：「經學文雅，亦漢之間、平也。」

translations.literal: Zheng said: "In classical learning and refined elegance, he is also like the Han dynasty's Jian and Ping."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng replied, "In scholarship and refinement he recalls the Han princes Liu Jian and Liu Ping."

sentences.zh: 由是寵遇彌厚，因令娶征女焉。

translations.literal: From this favored treatment grew ever thicker, and he was therefore made to marry Zheng's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter imperial favor toward Yuangui deepened, and the emperor had him marry Wei Zheng's daughter.

sentences.zh: 從太宗遊獵，遇群獸，命元軌射之，矢不虛發，太宗撫其背曰：「汝武藝過人，悵今無所施耳。

translations.literal: Following Taizong on a hunting excursion, they encountered a herd of beasts. He ordered Yuangui to shoot them; not an arrow was wasted. Taizong stroked his back and said: "Your martial skill surpasses others — I regret that now there is nowhere to deploy it.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunting expedition with Taizong they came upon a herd of game, and Taizong ordered Yuangui to shoot; every arrow found its mark. Taizong clapped him on the back and said, "Your martial prowess is extraordinary — it is a pity there is no longer a war in which to prove it.

sentences.zh: 當天下未定，我得汝豈不美乎！」

translations.literal: When the realm was not yet settled, would it not have been fine for me to have obtained you!"
translations.idiomatic: Had the empire still been unsettled, how splendid it would have been to put you in the field!

sentences.zh: 七年，拜壽州刺史，賜實封六百戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Shouzhou prefect and granted six hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed prefect of Shouzhou and granted a substantive fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，去職，毀瘠過禮，自後常衣布，示有終身之戚焉。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, he left office; his emaciation from grief exceeded the rites. From then on he always wore cloth, showing he had lifelong sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died, Yuangui left his post and mourned so severely that he wasted away beyond what ritual required; thereafter he wore only plain cloth, signaling grief he would never lay aside.

sentences.zh: 每至忌辰，輒數日不食。

translations.literal: Each time the anniversary of death arrived, he would for several days not eat.
translations.idiomatic: On each anniversary of his father's death he would fast for days on end.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封霍王，授絳州刺史，尋轉徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Prince of Huo, appointed Jiangzhou prefect, and soon transferred to Xuzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his title was changed to Prince of Huo; he was appointed prefect of Jiangzhou and soon transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 元軌前後為刺史，至州，唯閉閣讀書，吏事責成於長史、司馬，謹慎自守，與物無忤，為人不妄。

translations.literal: Yuangui, before and after serving as prefect, upon reaching the prefecture would only close the gate and read books; administrative affairs he entrusted to the chief administrator and vice administrator. He was cautious in self-restraint, had no conflict with others, and as a man was not reckless.
translations.idiomatic: In each prefectural posting Yuangui shut himself in his quarters to read, leaving daily administration to his chief and vice administrators; he was circumspect, offended no one, and never acted rashly.

sentences.zh: 在徐州，唯與處士劉玄平為布衣之交。

translations.literal: While at Xuzhou, he only with the reclusive scholar Liu Xuanping had the friendship of commoners in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou his sole intimate companion was the recluse Liu Xuanping, with whom he kept the easy friendship of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 人或問玄平王之長，玄平答曰：「無長。」

translations.literal: Someone asked Liu Xuanping about the prince's strengths; Liu Xuanping replied: "He has no strengths."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked Liu Xuanping what the prince did best, he answered, "Nothing in particular.

sentences.zh: 問者怪而復問之，玄平曰：「夫人有短，所以見其長。

translations.literal: The questioner wondered and asked again; Liu Xuanping said: "When a man has shortcomings, thereby one sees his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Puzzled, the man pressed him again. Liu Xuanping said, "We notice a man's strengths only because he has shortcomings somewhere.

sentences.zh: 至於霍王，無所不備，吾何以稱之哉？」

translations.literal: As for the Prince of Huo, there is nothing he lacks — how can I name his strengths?"
translations.idiomatic: But the Prince of Huo lacks nothing at all — what single virtue could I point to and call his forte?"

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶，為定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households, and he became Dingzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households, and he was appointed prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥來寇，元軌令開門偃旗，虜疑有伏，懼而宵遁。

translations.literal: When the Turks came to raid, Yuangui ordered the gates opened and banners lowered; the barbarians suspected an ambush, feared, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks raided the border, Yuangui had the city gates opened and banners lowered; the invaders, suspecting a trap, withdrew under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 州人李嘉運與賊連謀，事洩，高宗令收按其黨。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture, Li Jiayun, conspired with the bandits; the affair leaked out, and Gaozong ordered the arrest and investigation of his faction.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Li Jiayun was found to have colluded with the enemy; when the plot was exposed, Gaozong ordered a full roundup of his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 元軌以強寇在境，人心不安，惟殺嘉運，余無所及，因自劾違制。

translations.literal: Yuangui, because strong bandits were on the border and people's hearts were unsettled, only executed Jiayun and reached to no others, and therefore impeached himself for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: With powerful enemies still on the frontier and the populace unsettled, Yuangui executed only Jiayun and no one else, then submitted a self-accusation for exceeding his authority.

sentences.zh: 上覽表大悅，謂使曰：「朕亦悔之，向無王，則失定州矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and was greatly pleased, telling the envoy: "I too regret it — had it not been for the prince, we would have lost Dingzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong read the memorial with great satisfaction and told the messenger, "I had second thoughts myself — without the prince, we would have lost Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 有王文操遇賊，而二子鳳、賢遂以身蔽捍，文操獲全，二子皆死。

translations.literal: There was Wang Wencao who encountered bandits; his two sons Feng and Xian then used their bodies to shield and defend him. Wencao was preserved whole, and both sons died.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Wang Wencao was attacked by bandits; his sons Feng and Xian threw themselves between the blades and died, but their father was saved.

sentences.zh: 縣司抑而不申，元軌察知，遣使弔祭，表上其事，詔並贈朝散大夫，令加旌表。

translations.literal: The county office suppressed it and did not report upward. Yuangui detected this, sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice, memorialized the matter upward, and an edict posthumously granted both Court Gentleman for Dispersing Affairs and ordered additional commendation and public inscription.
translations.idiomatic: The county authorities had suppressed the report, but Yuangui learned of it, sent envoys to perform funeral rites, and memorialized the case; an edict posthumously ennobled both sons as Court Gentlemen for Dispersing Affairs and ordered a public commendation.

sentences.zh: 其禮賢愛善如此。

translations.literal: His honoring the worthy and loving goodness was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his regard for the worthy and the good.

sentences.zh: 後因入朝，屢上疏陳時政得失，多所匡益，高宗甚尊重之。

translations.literal: Later, because he entered court, he repeatedly submitted memorials stating the gains and losses of current government, correcting and benefiting in many ways; Gaozong greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: On later visits to court he repeatedly memorialized the throne on the failings and merits of current policy, offering much useful counsel, and Gaozong held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 及在外籓，朝廷每有大事，或密制問焉。

translations.literal: When he was in the outer fiefs, whenever the court had major affairs, it would sometimes secretly decree to inquire of him.
translations.idiomatic: While he held provincial posts, the court often sought his confidential opinion on weighty matters.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，與侍中劉齊賢等知山陵葬事，齊賢服其識練故事，每謂人曰：「非我輩所及也。」

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, together with Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Qixian and others he managed the mountain tomb burial affairs. Qixian admired his knowledge and mastery of precedent, and often told people: "This is not what our kind can reach."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Yuangui joined Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Qixian in overseeing the imperial burial; Qixian marveled at his mastery of ritual precedent and often said, "We cannot equal him.

sentences.zh: 元軌嘗使國令征封，令白：「請依諸國賦物貿易取利。」

translations.literal: Yuangui once had the state commandant levy the fief; the commandant reported: "I request, following other princedoms, to trade tribute goods for profit."
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui once ordered his princely steward to collect the fief revenues; the steward proposed trading the princedom's tribute goods for profit, as other princes did.

sentences.zh: 元軌曰：「汝為國令，當正吾失，反說吾以利耶！」

translations.literal: Yuangui said: "You serve as state commandant — you should correct my faults, yet instead you speak to me of profit!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui replied, "You are the princely steward — your duty is to correct my faults, not to counsel me toward profit!"

sentences.zh: 拒而不納。

translations.literal: He refused and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He rejected the proposal outright.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年，加位司徒，尋出為襄州刺史，轉青州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong he was given the additional rank of Minister of Education, and soon went out as Xiangzhou prefect, then transferred to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chuigong era he was promoted to Minister of Education, then dispatched as prefect of Xiangzhou and later transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，坐與越王貞連謀起兵，事覺，徙居黔州，仍令載以檻車，行至陳倉而死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on account of conspiring with Prince Zhen of Yue to raise troops, the affair was discovered; he was relocated to live in Qianzhou, and was still ordered carried in a caged cart; traveling to Chencang he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was implicated in the conspiracy with Prince Zhen of Yue to raise troops; when the plot was uncovered he was exiled to Qianzhou in a prison cart and died en route at Chencang.

sentences.zh: 有子七人。

translations.literal: He had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: Seven sons were born to him.

sentences.zh: 長子緒，最有才藝。

translations.literal: The eldest son Xu had the most talent and arts.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Xu was the most gifted.

sentences.zh: 上元中，封江都王，累除金州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangdu and repeatedly dismissed as Jinzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan period he was created Prince of Jiangdu and served successively as prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 重拱中，坐與裴承光交通被殺。

translations.literal: In the Chonggong era, on account of associating with Pei Chengguang he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chonggong era he was executed for dealings with Pei Chengguang.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，與元軌並追復爵位，仍封緒孫暉為嗣霍王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, together with Yuangui his title was posthumously restored, and Xu's grandson Hui was still enfeoffed as heir Prince of Huo.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong reign, Yuangui's rank was posthumously restored along with his honors, and Xu's grandson Hui was created heir to the Huo princedom.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jinglong he was given the additional title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jinglong era he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 開元中，左千牛員外將軍。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Left Supernumerary General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan period he served as Left Supernumerary General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 虢王鳳

translations.literal: Prince of Guo, Feng
translations.idiomatic: Feng, Prince of Guo

sentences.zh: 虢王鳳，高祖第十五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Feng of Guo was Gaozu's fifteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Feng of Guo was the fifteenth son of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 武德六年，封豳王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Wude era he was created Prince of Bin.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，授鄧州刺史，賜實封六百戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he was appointed Dengzhou prefect and granted six hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Zhenguan era he was appointed prefect of Dengzhou and granted a substantive fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十年，徙封虢王，歷虢、豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Guo, and successively served as Guo and Yu prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his title was changed to Prince of Guo, and he served in turn as prefect of Guo and Yu.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，累授青州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Linde he was repeatedly appointed Qingzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Linde era he was appointed prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上元元年薨，年五十二，贈司徒、揚州大都督，陪葬獻陵，謚曰莊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan he died, age fifty-two, posthumously granted Minister of Education and Yangzhou governor-general, buried with Xian Mausoleum, posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Shangyuan era at the age of fifty-two, was posthumously ennobled as Minister of Education and governor-general of Yangzhou, interred at Xian Mausoleum, and given the posthumous name Zhuang, "Solemn."

sentences.zh: 子平陽郡王翼嗣，官至光州刺史。

translations.literal: His son, Prince of Pingyang Commandery Yi, succeeded, and reached the office of Guangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, Prince of Pingyang Commandery, succeeded him and rose to prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Yonglong era.

sentences.zh: 子寓嗣，則天時失爵。

translations.literal: His son Yu succeeded; in Empress Wu's time he lost his title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu succeeded to the line but lost his title during Empress Wu's reign.

sentences.zh: 鳳第三子定襄郡公宏，則天初為曹州刺史。

translations.literal: Feng's third son, Duke of Dingxiang Commandery Hong, at the beginning of Empress Wu's reign was Cao prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's third son Hong, Duke of Dingxiang Commandery, served as prefect of Cao at the opening of Empress Wu's reign.

sentences.zh: 第五子東莞郡公融，少以武勇見知。

translations.literal: The fifth son, Duke of Dongguan Commandery Rong, when young was known for martial valor.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth son, Rong, Duke of Dongguan Commandery, won early renown for his martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，為申州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Chui Gong era he served as Shenzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chui Gong period he served as prefect of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，黃公譔將與越王貞通謀，深倚仗融，以為外助。

translations.literal: Earlier, Duke of Huang Fu was about to conspire with Prince of Yue Zhen, deeply relying on Rong as external support.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fu, Duke of Huang, was plotting with Prince Zhen of Yue, he placed great trust in Rong as an outside ally.

sentences.zh: 時詔追諸親赴都，融私使問其所親成均助教高子貢曰：「可入朝以否？」

translations.literal: At that time an edict summoned all imperial kin to the capital. Rong secretly sent someone to ask his close associate, Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education Gao Zigong, saying, "May one enter court or not?
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered all royal relatives to report to the capital, Rong secretly sent a messenger to ask his confidant Gao Zigong, assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education: "Is it safe to go to court?

sentences.zh: 子貢報曰：「來必取死。」

translations.literal: Zigong replied, "If you come you will surely meet death."
translations.idiomatic: Zigong answered, "If you go, you will certainly be killed."

sentences.zh: 融乃稱疾不朝，以俟諸籓期。

translations.literal: Rong then claimed illness and did not attend court, waiting for the princely domains' appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: Rong thereupon pleaded illness and stayed away from court, waiting for the day when the princes were to rise together.

sentences.zh: 及得越王貞起兵書，倉卒不能相應，為僚吏所逼，不獲已而奏之，於是擢授銀青光祿大夫，行太子右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: When he received Prince of Yue Zhen's letter calling troops to arms, in haste he could not respond in concert. Pressed by his staff officials, with no choice he reported it. Thereupon he was promoted and appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent's Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhen of Yue's call to arms reached him, he could not respond in time. His subordinate officials pressed him, and he had no choice but to report the plot to the throne. He was then promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and appointed acting Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent's Tutor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為支黨所引，被誅。

translations.literal: Before long, implicated by affiliated partisans, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was implicated through his associates and put to death.

sentences.zh: 子徹，神龍元年襲封東莞郡公。

translations.literal: His son Che, in the first year of Shenlong, inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Dongguan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Che inherited the title of Duke of Dongguan Commandery in the first year of the Shenlong era.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，繼密王元曉，改為嗣密王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he succeeded Prince of Mi Yuanxiao and was changed to Heir Prince of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he succeeded Yuanxiao, Prince of Mi, and was redesignated Heir Prince of Mi.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改封濮陽郡王，歷宗正卿、金紫光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Puyang Commandery. He successively served as Director of the Imperial Clan and Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year his title was changed to Prince of Puyang Commandery. He later served as Director of the Imperial Clan and as Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness before his death.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，封鳳嫡孫邕為嗣虢王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Feng's eldest grandson by the principal wife, Yong, was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong era, Yong, Feng's eldest grandson by the principal wife, was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Guo.

sentences.zh: 邕娶韋庶人妹為妻，由是中宗時特承寵異，轉秘書監，俄又改封汴王，開府置僚屬。

translations.literal: Yong took Empress Wei's younger sister as wife. Because of this, in Zhongzong's time he especially received favor and distinction. He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, and soon his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Bian, opening a princely establishment and appointing staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yong married the younger sister of Empress Wei, and under Zhongzong he enjoyed exceptional favor. He was appointed Director of the Secretariat, then soon redesignated Prince of Bian with a princely establishment and full staff.

sentences.zh: 月餘而韋氏敗，邕揮刃截其妻首，以至於朝，深為物議所鄙。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month the Wei clan fell. Yong swung a blade and cut off his wife's head, then brought it to court. He was deeply despised in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later, when the Wei faction fell, Yong drew a blade and severed his wife's head, then carried it to court—a deed that earned him widespread contempt.

sentences.zh: 貶沁州刺史，不知州事，削封邑。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Qinzhou prefect, denied charge of prefectural affairs, and his fief was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to prefect of Qinzhou but stripped of administrative authority and had his fief reduced.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，復嗣虢王，還封二百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he was restored as Heir Prince of Guo, and two hundred households of fief were returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun he was restored as Heir Prince of Guo, and two hundred fief households were returned to him.

sentences.zh: 累遷衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 開元十五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 子巨嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Ju succeeded; there is a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ju succeeded to the line; he has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 道王元慶

translations.literal: Prince of Dao, Yuangqing
translations.idiomatic: Yuangqing, Prince of Dao

sentences.zh: 鄧王元裕

translations.literal: Prince of Deng, Yuanyu
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu, Prince of Deng

sentences.zh: 舒王元名

translations.literal: Prince of Shu, Yuanming
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming, Prince of Shu

sentences.zh: 舒王元名，高祖第十八子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Yuanming was Gaozu's eighteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming, Prince of Shu, was the eighteenth son of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 年十歲時，高祖在大安宮，太宗晨夕使尚宮起居送珍饌，元名保傅等謂元名曰：「尚宮品秩高者，見宜拜之。」

translations.literal: When he was ten years old, Gaozu was in Daima Palace. Taizong morning and evening sent palace ladies to inquire after his health and deliver fine foods. Yuanming's tutors and others said to Yuanming, "Palace ladies of high rank and station—when you see them you ought to bow.
translations.idiomatic: When he was ten, Gaozu was living in Daima Palace, and Taizong sent palace ladies each morning and evening to inquire after his health and bring delicacies. Yuanming's tutors told him, "When you meet a senior palace lady, you should bow to her.

sentences.zh: 元名曰：「此我二哥家婢也，何用拜為？」

translations.literal: Yuanming said, "These are my second elder brother's household maidservants—why bow to them?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming replied, "They are only my second brother's household servants—why should I bow to them?"

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而壯之，曰：「此真我弟也。」

translations.literal: Taizong heard of it and admired him, saying, "This is truly my brother."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard this, he was impressed and said, "That is a true brother of mine."

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，封譙王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he received enfeoffment as Prince of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he was created Prince of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 十一年，徙封舒王，賜實封八百戶，拜壽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Shu, granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households, and appointed Shouzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year his title was changed to Prince of Shu, he received a substantive fief of eight hundred households, and he was appointed prefect of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 後歷滑、許、鄭三州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as prefect of Huazhou, Xuzhou, and Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as prefect of Huazhou, Xuzhou, and Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶，轉石州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households, and he was transferred to Shizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households, and he was transferred to prefect of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 元名性高潔，罕問家人產業，朝夕矜莊，門庭清肅，常誡其子豫章王亶等曰：「籓王所乏者，不慮無錢財官職，但勉行善事，忠孝持身，此吾志也。」

translations.literal: Yuanming's nature was lofty and pure. He rarely inquired about his household's property. Morning and evening he maintained dignified reserve; his gate and courtyard were clear and solemn. He often admonished his sons, Prince of Yuzhang Dan and others, saying, "What a prince lacks is not to be feared as lacking wealth or official posts—only strive to do good deeds and uphold loyalty and filial piety in your persons. This is my aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming was a man of lofty integrity who rarely concerned himself with household wealth. He maintained a grave and dignified bearing from morning to night, and his household was always orderly and austere. He often warned his sons, including Dan, Prince of Yuzhang: "A prince need never worry about lacking money or office; what matters is to do good, and to conduct yourselves with loyalty and filial piety. That is my aim.

sentences.zh: 及亶為江州刺史，以善政聞，高宗手敕褒美元名，以賞其義方之訓。

translations.literal: When Dan served as Jiangzhou prefect and was known for good governance, Gaozong personally drafted an edict praising Yuanming, to reward his righteous instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan served as prefect of Jiangzhou and won a reputation for good governance, Emperor Gaozong issued a personal edict praising Yuanming to reward his upright teaching of his sons.

sentences.zh: 高宗每欲授元名大州刺史，固辭曰：「忝預籓戚，豈以州郡戶口為仕進之資？」

translations.literal: Whenever Gaozong wished to appoint Yuanming to a great prefecture, he firmly declined, saying, "I am unworthy to share in princely kinship—how could I take a prefecture's households and population as capital for advancement in office?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Gaozong tried to appoint Yuanming to a large prefecture, he firmly refused, saying, "As a member of the imperial house, how could I treat a prefecture's population as a stepping-stone to higher office?

sentences.zh: 辭情懇到，故在石州二十年，賞玩林泉，有塵外之意。

translations.literal: His declining words were earnest and sincere. Therefore at Shizhou for twenty years he enjoyed forests and springs, with a mind beyond the dust of the world.
translations.idiomatic: His refusal was so earnest and sincere that he remained at Shizhou for twenty years, delighting in its woods and streams with the spirit of a man who had stepped beyond worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 垂拱年，除青州刺史，又除鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Chui Gong years he was appointed Qingzhou prefect, and again appointed Zhengzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chui Gong period he was appointed prefect of Qingzhou, and later prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 州境鄰接都畿，諸王及帝戚蒞官者，或有不檢攝家人，為百姓所苦。

translations.literal: The prefecture's territory bordered the capital region. Princes and imperial kin who came to hold office there sometimes failed to restrain their households, causing suffering to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Because the prefecture bordered the capital region, princes and imperial relatives who served there often failed to control their households, to the great distress of the common people.

sentences.zh: 及元名到，大革其弊。

translations.literal: When Yuanming arrived, he greatly reformed these abuses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanming took office, he thoroughly reformed these abuses.

sentences.zh: 轉滑州刺史，政理如在鄭州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huazhou prefect; his governance was as at Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Huazhou, he governed with the same effectiveness he had shown at Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋加授司空。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 永昌年，與子亶俱為丘神勣所陷，被殺。

translations.literal: In the Yongchang years he and his son Dan were both framed by Qiu Shenji and were killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchang period he and his son Dan were both framed by Qiu Shenji and put to death.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，贈司徒，復其官爵，仍令以禮改葬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was posthumously granted Minister of Education, his offices and titles were restored, and he was ordered reburied according to rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong era he was posthumously ennobled as Minister of Education, his offices and titles were restored, and he was reinterred with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 亶子津為嗣舒王。

translations.literal: Dan's son Jin became Heir Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's son Jin succeeded as Heir Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jinglong he was additionally granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jinglong he was additionally appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 開元中，左威衛將軍，卒。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he served as General of the Left Majestic Guard, then died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he served as General of the Left Majestic Guard before his death.

sentences.zh: 子萬嗣，天寶二年卒。

translations.literal: His son Wan succeeded; in the second year of Tianbao he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wan succeeded to the line and died in the second year of the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 子藻嗣，天寶九載，封嗣舒王。

translations.literal: His son Zao succeeded; in the ninth year of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zao succeeded and was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Shu in the ninth year of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 魯王靈夔

translations.literal: Prince of Lu, Lingkui
translations.idiomatic: Lingkui, Prince of Lu

sentences.zh: 魯王靈夔，高祖第十九子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Lu Lingkui was Gaozu's nineteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Lingkui, Prince of Lu, was the nineteenth son of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 少有美譽，善音律，好學，工草隸，與同母兄韓王元嘉特相友愛。

translations.literal: In youth he had a fine reputation. He was skilled in music, loved learning, and was adept at cursive and clerical script. With his elder brother of the same mother, Prince of Han Yuanjia, he was especially close and affectionate.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed a fine reputation from youth. Skilled in music, devoted to learning, and accomplished in cursive and clerical calligraphy, he was especially close to his elder uterine brother Yuanjia, Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，封魏王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he received enfeoffment as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he was created Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封燕王，賜實封八百戶，授幽州都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Yan, he was granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households, and appointed Area Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his title was changed to Prince of Yan, he received a substantive fief of eight hundred households, and he was appointed area commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，改封魯王，授兗州都督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Lu, and he was appointed Area Commander of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year his title was changed to Prince of Lu, and he was appointed area commander of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年，轉隆州刺史，後歷絳、滑、定等州刺史，太子太師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui he was transferred to Longzhou prefect. Later he successively served as prefect of Jiangzhou, Huazhou, and Dingzhou, and as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yonghui he was transferred to prefect of Longzhou. He later served in turn as prefect of Jiangzhou, Huazhou, and Dingzhou, and as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年，授邢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chui Gong he was appointed Xingzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chui Gong he was appointed prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，與兄元嘉子黃公譔結謀，欲起兵應接越王貞父子，事洩，配流振州，自縊而死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he joined in plotting with his elder brother Yuanjia's son Duke of Huang Fu, intending to raise troops in response to Prince of Yue Zhen and his son. The affair leaked out. He was sentenced to exile at Zhenzhou and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he plotted with Fu, Duke of Huang, son of his elder brother Yuanjia, to raise troops in support of Prince Zhen of Yue and his son. When the plot was exposed, he was exiled to Zhenzhou and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 有二子：長子銑，封清河王。

translations.literal: He had two sons: the eldest, Xian, was enfeoffed as Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder, Xian, was enfeoffed as Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 次子藹，封范陽王，歷右散騎常侍，為酷吏所陷。

translations.literal: The second son, Ai, was enfeoffed as Prince of Fanyang, successively served as Right Regular Attendant, and was framed by harsh officials.
translations.idiomatic: The younger, Ai, was enfeoffed as Prince of Fanyang, served as Right Regular Attendant, and was framed by the harsh officials.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追復靈夔官爵，仍令以禮改葬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong Lingkui's offices and titles were posthumously restored, and he was ordered reburied according to rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong era Lingkui's offices and titles were posthumously restored, and he was reinterred with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 封藹子道堅為嗣魯王。

translations.literal: Ai's son Daojian received enfeoffment as Heir Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Daojian, son of Ai, succeeded as Heir Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 性嚴整，雖在閨門，造次必於莊敬。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and orderly. Even within the women's quarters, in every hasty moment he maintained solemn respect.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of strict and orderly character who maintained solemn propriety even in the inner quarters of his household.

sentences.zh: 少年佐郡，聲實已彰。

translations.literal: In youth while assisting in a commandery, his reputation and substance were already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a young man assisting in prefectural administration, his reputation for ability was already well established.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年，加銀青光祿大夫，歷果、隴、吉、冀、洺、汾、滄等七州刺史，國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jinglong he was additionally granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, successively served as prefect of Guozhou, Longzhou, Jizhou, Jizhou, Mingzhou, Fenzhou, and Cangzhou—the seven prefectures—and as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jinglong he was additionally appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. He served in turn as prefect of Guozhou, Longzhou, Jizhou, Jizhou, Mingzhou, Fenzhou, and Cangzhou—seven prefectures in all—and as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 開元二十二年，兼檢校魏州刺史，未行，改汴州刺史、河南道採訪使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan he was additionally appointed acting Inspector of Weizhou. Before departing he was changed to Bianzhou prefect and Commissioner for Circuit Inspection of Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan he was additionally appointed acting inspector of Weizhou, but before he could take up the post he was reassigned as prefect of Bianzhou and Henan Circuit inspection commissioner.

sentences.zh: 此州都會，水陸輻湊，實曰膏腴，道堅特以清毅聞。

translations.literal: This prefecture was a great metropolis where land and water routes converged; it was truly rich and fertile. Daojian was especially known for purity and firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Bianzhou was a great metropolis where land and water routes converged—a truly wealthy and fertile region—and Daojian won particular renown for his integrity and firmness of character.

sentences.zh: 入為宗正卿，卒。

translations.literal: He entered court service as Director of the Imperial Clan, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Director of the Imperial Clan and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子宇嗣，二十九年，封嗣魯王。

translations.literal: His son Yu succeeded; in the twenty-ninth year he was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu succeeded to the line and was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Lu in the twenty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，從幸巴蜀，為右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he followed the emperor on the journey to Ba-Shu and served as General of the Right Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide he accompanied the emperor to Ba-Shu and served as General of the Right Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，皇太子封為魯王，改宇嗣鄒王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying the crown prince received enfeoffment as Prince of Lu, and Yu's line of succession was changed to Prince of Zou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying the crown prince was created Prince of Lu, and Yu was reassigned to succeed as Prince of Zou.

sentences.zh: 道堅弟道邃，中興初，封戴國公。

translations.literal: Daojian's younger brother Daosui, at the beginning of the Restoration, was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Daojian's younger brother Daosui was enfeoffed as Duke of Dai at the beginning of the Restoration.

sentences.zh: 以恭默自守，修山東婚姻故事，頻任清列。

translations.literal: Maintaining himself in respectful silence, he upheld the marriage traditions of the Eastern Mountains and was repeatedly appointed to pure, exalted ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He kept to a modest and reticent reserve, upheld the marriage customs of the great Shandong clans, and was repeatedly appointed to prestigious offices.

sentences.zh: 天寶中為右丞，大理、宗正二卿，卒。
