translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he served as Right Vice Director, and as Chancellor of the Court of Judicial Review and Director of the Imperial Clan, then died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he served as Right Vice Director and as Chancellor of the Court of Judicial Review and Director of the Imperial Clan before his death.

sentences.zh: 江王元祥

translations.literal: Prince of Jiang, Yuanxiang
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiang, Prince of Jiang

sentences.zh: 江王元祥，高祖第二十子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiang Yuanxiang was Gaozu's twentieth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiang, Prince of Jiang, was the twentieth son of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，封許王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he received enfeoffment as Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he was created Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，徙封江王，授蘇州刺史，賜實封八百戶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Jiang, appointed Suzhou prefect, and granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year his title was changed to Prince of Jiang, he was appointed prefect of Suzhou, and he received a substantive fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，又歷金、鄜、鄭三州刺史。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time he again successively served as prefect of Jinzhou, Fuzhou, and Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he served in turn as prefect of Jinzhou, Fuzhou, and Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 性貪鄙，多聚金寶，營求無厭，為人吏所患。

translations.literal: His nature was greedy and base. He amassed much gold and treasure and pursued gain without satiety, causing distress to officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: He was greedy and base by nature, hoarded gold and jewels, and pursued profit without limit, to the great distress of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 時滕王元嬰、蔣王惲、虢王鳳亦稱貪暴，有授得其府官者，以比嶺南惡處，為之語曰：「寧向儋、崖、振、白，不事江、滕、蔣、虢。」

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Teng Yuanying, Prince of Jiang Yun, and Prince of Guo Feng were also called greedy and violent. Those appointed to offices in their establishments compared them to evil places in Lingnan, and made a saying: "Better to go to Dan, Ya, Zhen, and Bai than to serve Jiang, Teng, Jiang, and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanying of Teng, Prince Yun of Jiang, and Prince Feng of Guo were likewise notorious for greed and cruelty. Men appointed to posts in their households compared service under them to exile in the worst prefectures of Lingnan, and a saying circulated: "Better to be sent to Dan, Ya, Zhen, or Bai than to serve Jiang, Teng, Jiang, or Guo.

sentences.zh: 元祥體質洪大，腰帶十圍，飲啖亦兼數人，其時韓王元嘉、虢王鳳、魏王恭狀貌亦偉，不逮於元祥。

translations.literal: Yuanxiang's bodily frame was vast; his waist belt was ten arm-spans around, and in eating and drinking he consumed as much as several men. At that time Prince of Han Yuanjia, Prince of Guo Feng, and Prince of Wei Gong also had imposing stature, but did not match Yuanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiang was a man of enormous build—his waist measured ten arm-spans around, and he ate and drank enough for several men. Yuanjia, Prince of Han, Feng, Prince of Guo, and Gong, Prince of Wei, were also imposing in stature, but none matched Yuanxiang.

sentences.zh: 又眇一目。

translations.literal: He also had one eye that was blind.
translations.idiomatic: He was also blind in one eye.

sentences.zh: 永隆元年薨，贈司徒、并州大都督，陪葬獻陵，謚曰安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonglong he died, posthumously granted Minister of Education and Bingzhou governor-general, buried with Xian Mausoleum, posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Yonglong era, was posthumously ennobled as Minister of Education and governor-general of Bingzhou, interred at Xian Mausoleum, and given the posthumous name An, "Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 子永嘉王晫，永隆中，為復州刺史。

translations.literal: His son, Prince of Yongjia Zhuo, in the Yonglong years served as Fuzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuo, Prince of Yongjia, served as prefect of Fuzhou during the Yonglong period.

sentences.zh: 以禽獸其行，賜死於家。

translations.literal: Because his conduct was beastly, he was granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: Because his conduct was beastly, he was ordered to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 中興初，元祥子鉅鹿郡公晃子欽嗣江王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration, Yuanxiang's son Duke of Julu Commandery Huang's son Qin succeeded as Prince of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Restoration, Qin, son of Huang, Duke of Julu Commandery and son of Yuanxiang, succeeded as Prince of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年，加銀青光祿大夫，娶王仁皎女，至千牛將軍，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jinglong he was additionally granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, took Wang Renjiao's daughter as wife, reached General of the Thousand-Ox Guard, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jinglong he was additionally appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, married the daughter of Wang Renjiao, rose to General of the Thousand-Ox Guard, and died.

sentences.zh: 密王元曉

translations.literal: Prince of Mi, Yuanxiao
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiao, Prince of Mi

sentences.zh: 密王元曉，高祖第二十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Mi Yuanxiao was Gaozu's twenty-first son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiao, Prince of Mi, was the twenty-first son of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年受封。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He received his princely title in the fifth year of Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 九年，授虢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Guozhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，賜實封八百戶。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he received a substantive fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加滿千戶，轉澤州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year it was increased to a full thousand households, and he was transferred to Zezhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his fief was raised to one thousand households, and he was transferred to prefect of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，除宣州刺史，後歷徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui he was appointed Xuanzhou prefect; later he successively served as Xuzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yonghui he was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou, and later served as prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 上元三年薨，贈司徒、揚州都督，陪葬獻陵，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan he died, posthumously granted Minister of Education and Yangzhou governor-general, buried with Xian Mausoleum, posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Shangyuan era, was posthumously ennobled as Minister of Education and governor-general of Yangzhou, interred at Xian Mausoleum, and given the posthumous name Zhen, "Upright."

sentences.zh: 子南安王穎嗣。

translations.literal: His son, Prince of Nan'an Ying, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying, Prince of Nan'an, succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，封穎弟亮子曇為嗣密王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Ying's younger brother Liang's son Tan was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong era, Tan, son of Ying's younger brother Liang, was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Mi.

sentences.zh: 滕王元嬰

translations.literal: Prince of Teng, Yuanying
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying, Prince of Teng

sentences.zh: 滕王元嬰，高祖第二十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Teng Yuanying was Gaozu's twenty-second son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying, Prince of Teng, was the twenty-second son of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十三年受封。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan he received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He received his princely title in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 十五年，賜實封八百戶，授金州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households and appointed Jinzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he received a substantive fief of eight hundred households and was appointed prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，元嬰頗驕縱逸游，動作失度，高宗與書誡之曰：「王地在宗枝，寄深磐石，幼聞《詩》、《禮》，夙承義訓。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era Yuanying was rather arrogant, indulging in roaming and idleness, his conduct departing from proper measure. Gaozong wrote him a letter of admonition, saying: "My lord, your place lies within the imperial branch, entrusted like bedrock upon which the realm rests. In youth you studied the Odes and the Rites, and from early on received righteous instruction.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era Yuanying grew arrogant and dissolute, his conduct increasingly unbecoming. Gaozong sent him a letter of admonition: "Prince, you stand among the imperial kinsmen, a pillar on whom the realm is meant to rest. From childhood you were steeped in the Odes and the Rites and reared in proper moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 實冀孜孜無怠，漸以成德，豈謂不遵軌轍，踰越典章。

translations.literal: I truly hoped you would labor without slackening and gradually complete your virtue — who would have thought you would fail to follow the wheel-tracks and overstep ritual statutes?
translations.idiomatic: I had truly hoped you would labor without slackening and gradually ripen into virtue. I never imagined you would stray from the proper path and violate the statutes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 且城池作固，以備不虞，關鑰閉開，須有常准。

translations.literal: Moreover ramparts and moats are made strong to guard against the unforeseen; barriers and locks, closed or opened, must have fixed standards.
translations.idiomatic: City walls and moats are fortified to meet unforeseen danger; the gates must be opened and shut according to fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 鳩合散樂，並集府僚，嚴關夜開，非復一度。

translations.literal: You gather together itinerant musicians, assembling prefectural officials, and the stern passes open at night — not merely once.
translations.idiomatic: You summon roaming musicians, crowd your prefectural staff together, and throw open the fortified gates by night — not once, but again and again.

sentences.zh: 遏密之悲，尚纏比屋，王以此情事，何遽紛紜？

translations.literal: The grief of "suppressing secret music" still binds every household — yet you, my lord, with such matters at hand, how can you so hastily throw things into turmoil?
translations.idiomatic: The nation's mourning still binds every household in sorrow — how can you, with such grief upon the realm, so hastily stir up this clamor?

sentences.zh: 又巡省百姓，本觀風問俗，遂乃驅率老幼，借狗求置，志從禽之娛，忽黎元之重。

translations.literal: Again, in touring to inspect the common people — which is fundamentally to observe customs and inquire into manners — you thereupon drive and lead old and young, borrowing dogs and demanding their provision, your will bent to the pleasure of hunting birds, neglecting the weight of the black-headed masses.
translations.idiomatic: When you tour the countryside you are meant to observe local customs — yet you drive out old and young alike, borrow hunting dogs from them, and fix your heart on fowling while forgetting what the people mean to the realm.

sentences.zh: 時方農要，屢出畋游，以彈彈人，將為笑樂。

translations.literal: When farming is at its most crucial season you repeatedly go out hunting, using pellets to shoot at people, taking it as a source of laughter.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the farming season you go hunting again and again, shooting people with pellet-bows for your amusement.

sentences.zh: 取適之方，亦應多緒，何必此事，方得為娛？

translations.literal: The means of taking pleasure ought also to have many topics — why must it be this affair before there can be entertainment?
translations.idiomatic: There are countless ways to take one's pleasures — why must you choose this alone for your diversion?

sentences.zh: 晉靈虐主，未可取則。

translations.literal: Duke Ling of Jin maltreated his lord — he must not be taken as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ling of Jin abused his sovereign — he is no example to follow.

sentences.zh: 趙孝文趨走小人，張四又倡優賤隸，王親與博戲，極為輕脫，一府官僚，何所瞻望？

translations.literal: Zhao Xiaowen is a petty man who runs on errands; Zhang Si is moreover a base performer and menial of the entertainment house — yet my lord personally gambles with them, to an extreme of light impropriety. What are the officials of your entire establishment to look up to?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiaowen is a runner in your household, and Zhang Si a lowborn actor — yet you gamble with them yourself with scandalous abandon. What are the officers of your prefecture to take as their model?

sentences.zh: 凝寒方甚，以雪埋人，虐物既深，何以為樂？

translations.literal: When freezing cold is at its height you bury people in snow; when cruelty toward creatures runs so deep, what can serve as pleasure?
translations.idiomatic: In the dead of winter you bury people in snow. When cruelty runs this deep, what pleasure can remain in it?

sentences.zh: 家人奴僕，侮弄官人，至於此事，彌不可長。

translations.literal: Household retainers and slaves insult and toy with government officers; as for this matter, it all the more must not be allowed to grow.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants bully and mock your officials — conduct like this must not be indulged further.

sentences.zh: 朕以王骨肉至親，不能致王於法，令與王下上考，以愧王心。

translations.literal: I, considering that you are bone-and-flesh kin of the closest degree, cannot bring you before the law; I order that you be given the lowest grade of merit review, to shame your heart.
translations.idiomatic: Because you are my nearest kin by blood, I cannot bring you to trial; I assign you the lowest merit rating instead, that shame may move your heart.

sentences.zh: 人之有過，貴在能改，國有憲章，私恩難再。

translations.literal: When people have faults, what is prized is the ability to reform. The state has its constitutional statutes — private favor can hardly be granted again.
translations.idiomatic: When one errs, what matters is the will to amend. The realm has its laws — private indulgence cannot be extended twice.

sentences.zh: 興言及此，慚嘆盈懷。」

translations.literal: Raising words to this topic, shame and sighs fill the breast."
translations.idiomatic: As I speak of this, shame and sorrow overflow my heart."

sentences.zh: 三年，遷蘇州刺史，尋轉洪州都督。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Suzhou prefect, and soon thereafter made Area Commander of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to prefect of Suzhou, and soon after was appointed area commander of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 又數犯憲章，削邑戶及親事帳內之半，於滁州安置。

translations.literal: Again he repeatedly violated the constitutional statutes; his fief households and half of his personal accounts for domestic affairs were cut, and he was settled at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He violated the statutes again and again; his fief households and half his personal retainers were struck from the rolls, and he was resettled at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後起授壽州刺史，轉隆州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was restored and appointed Shouzhou prefect, then transferred to Longzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored to office as prefect of Shouzhou, then transferred to Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘道元年，加開府儀同三司，兼梁州都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongdao he was additionally granted Honorary Grand Preceptor with the status equal to the Three Excellencies and appointed concurrent Area Commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongdao he was further created Honorary Grand Preceptor of Equivalence to the Three Excellencies and appointed concurrent area commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 文明元年薨，贈司徒、冀州都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wenming he died; posthumously he was given Grand Tutor and Area Commander of Jizhou, and buried by accompaniment at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Wenming and was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor and area commander of Jizhou, with burial at Xianling by imperial accompaniment.

sentences.zh: 子長樂王循琦嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xunqi, Prince of Changle, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was succeeded by his son Xunqi, Prince of Changle.

sentences.zh: 兄弟六人，垂拱中並陷詔獄。

translations.literal: Six brothers — all in the Chui Gong era fell into the imperial prison on edict.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons — all six were imprisoned on imperial warrant during the Chui Gong era.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以循琦弟循琣子涉嗣滕王，本名茂宗，狀貌類胡而豐碩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, She, son of Xunqi's younger brother Xunbi, succeeded as Prince of Teng; his original name was Maozong, his appearance resembling that of the Hu peoples and being full and massive.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong era She, son of Xunbi, younger brother of Xunqi, succeeded as Prince of Teng. Born Maozong, he had a husky, foreign-looking build and a massive frame.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，加銀青光祿大夫，左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan he was additionally granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and made General of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan he was created Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and appointed General of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，淮安郡別駕，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he served as Vice Prefect of Huai'an Commandery, then died.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he served as vice prefect of Huai'an and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子湛然嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhanran succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was succeeded by his son Zhanran.

sentences.zh: 十一載，封滕王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Teng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was created Prince of Teng.

sentences.zh: 十五載，從幸蜀，除左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed on the journey of imperial fortune to Shu and was appointed General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he accompanied the emperor to Shu and was appointed General of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：一人元良，萬國以貞。

translations.literal: The historian says: When one man is the primordial good heir, the ten thousand states thereby stand upright.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When a single heir stands firm as the state's foundation, every realm under heaven finds its stability.

sentences.zh: 若明異重離，道非出震，雖居嫡長，寧固钅其鎡！

translations.literal: If brightness differs from Double Li, and the Way is not that of Emerging Thunder, though one occupies the position of legitimate eldest son, how could the heir be secured!
translations.idiomatic: If his virtue falls short of the heir's proper brilliance, if he lacks the moral force of the destined successor, then though he ranks as eldest son by birth, how can the crown prince's place be made secure?

sentences.zh: 況當開創之初，未見太平之兆。

translations.literal: Moreover this was precisely when the foundation had just been laid — one had not yet seen omens of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: And this was the hour of the dynasty's founding, when no sign yet pointed toward enduring peace.

sentences.zh: 建成殘忍，豈主鬯之才；

translations.literal: Jiancheng was cruel — how could he possess the talent to tend the libation grain?
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng was cruel — he lacked the talent to tend the ancestral altar.

sentences.zh: 元吉凶狂，有覆巢之跡。

translations.literal: Yuanji was sinister and wildly violent, with traces of overturning the nest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was vicious and wildly violent, with the makings of one who would overturn the nest and destroy his kin.

sentences.zh: 若非太宗逆取順守，積德累功，何以致三百年之延洪、二十帝之纂嗣？

translations.literal: If it had not been for Taizong's seizing against the current and governing in accord with it, accumulating virtue and piling up merit, how could one have brought about three hundred years of extended magnificence and twenty emperors succeeding the line?
translations.idiomatic: Had Taizong not taken power by force yet held it through righteous rule, building virtue upon virtue and merit upon merit, how could the dynasty have endured three hundred years and passed the succession through twenty emperors?

sentences.zh: 或堅持小節，必虧大猷，欲比秦二世、隋煬帝，亦不及矣。

translations.literal: Were they to cling stubbornly to minor integrity, they would necessarily impair the great design; to wish to compare them with the Second Emperor of Qin or Emperor Yang of Sui — they do not even reach that level.
translations.idiomatic: Even when they clung to minor proprieties they forfeited the greater design; to compare them with the Second Emperor of Qin or Emperor Yang of Sui would be to overrate them.

sentences.zh: 元嘉修身，元軌無短，元裕名理，元名高潔，靈夔嚴整，皆有封冊之名，而無磐石之固。

translations.literal: Yuanjia cultivated his person, Yuangui had no shortcomings, Yuanyu mastered the principles of names, Yuanming was lofty in purity, Lingkui stern and ordered — all had the fame of enfeoffed patents, yet lacked the solidity of bedrock.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia cultivated his person, Yuangui was without serious flaw, Yuanyu excelled in philosophical disputation, Yuanming was lofty in purity, and Lingkui was stern and orderly — all bore patent princely titles, yet none possessed bedrock solidity.

sentences.zh: 武氏之亂，或連頸被刑；

translations.literal: In the turmoil of the Wu clan, some were linked neck-to-neck and put to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil of the Wu clan, some were led to execution in chains, one after another.

sentences.zh: 奸臣擅權，則束手為制。

translations.literal: When treacherous ministers monopolized power, then with bound hands they were made subject.
translations.idiomatic: When treacherous ministers seized power, they could only fold their hands and submit.

sentences.zh: 其望本枝百世也，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: To look upon the hope that the stem-branch line would endure a hundred generations — is it not also difficult?
translations.idiomatic: To expect the imperial branch to flourish for a hundred generations — was that not a vain hope?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：有功曰祖，有德曰宗。

translations.literal: The encomium says: He who has merit is called "ancestor"; he who has virtue is called "forebear."
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: "He who achieves merit is called zu; he who embodies virtue is called zong."

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉，實為二凶。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji were truly the two villains.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji were veritable twin fiends.

sentences.zh: 中外交構，人神不容。

translations.literal: Within and without they plotted mutually — neither men nor spirits could tolerate them.
translations.idiomatic: They conspired within and without the court — neither men nor spirits could abide them.

sentences.zh: 用晦而明，殷憂啟聖。

translations.literal: Using obscurity yet attaining brightness, deep sorrow giving birth to sageliness.
translations.idiomatic: From adversity came clarity; through deep grief arose the sage.

sentences.zh: 運屬文皇，功成守正。

translations.literal: Fortune rested with the Literary Emperor; merit completed, he guarded the upright.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate fell to the Literary Emperor, who achieved the work of founding and then held firm to righteousness.

sentences.zh: 善惡既分，社稷乃定。

translations.literal: Once good and evil were divided, the altar of state was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once good and evil were separated, the altars of land and grain stood secure.

sentences.zh: 盤維封建，本枝茂盛。

translations.literal: The entwining girders of enfeoffment and feudal investiture — the stem-branch flourished luxuriantly.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal lords were arrayed like a fortress of entwined roots, and the imperial branch flourished lushly.

sentences.zh: 元嘉、元軌，修身慎行。

translations.literal: Yuanjia, Yuangui — they cultivated the person and were cautious in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia and Yuangui cultivated their persons and walked with careful virtue.

sentences.zh: 元裕、元名，行簡居正。

translations.literal: Yuanyu, Yuanming — their conduct was simple and they dwelt in the upright.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu and Yuanming lived simply and held themselves with rectitude.

sentences.zh: 犬牙不固，武氏易姓。

translations.literal: The dog-teeth pattern was not solid; the Wu clan changed the imperial surname.
translations.idiomatic: When the interlocking defenses failed, the Wu usurpers changed the dynasty's very surname.

sentences.zh: 既無兵民，若拘陷阱。

translations.literal: Since they lacked both troops and people, it was as if bound in a pit-trap.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of soldiers and subjects, they were like captives in a pitfall.

sentences.zh: 敢告後人，無或失政。

translations.literal: I dare inform those who come after — let none lose good governance.
translations.idiomatic: I warn those who follow: let no prince neglect the duties of rule.
